title: Enterprise AI and Machine Learning for Managers​
summary: This article introduces an eBook titled "Enterprise AI and Machine Learning for Managers," designed to provide frontline managers with a practical understanding of AI/ML. The book aims to equip managers with the knowledge to identify high-impact AI use cases, collaborate effectively with data scientists, and deploy AI/ML into production to gain a competitive advantage. Written by former McKinsey consultant and professor Nikhil Krishnan, the guide focuses on helping managers understand AI science, measure success, and build strong data science teams.

title: 8x8 Deploys XCaaS to 1,500 Hounslow Borough Council Employees
summary: 8x8 has deployed its XCaaS platform to 1,500 employees at Hounslow Borough Council, integrating Unified Communications as a Service (UCaaS) and Contact Center as a Service (CCaaS) with Microsoft Teams. This deployment aims to simplify communications, enhance efficiency for staff across various departments, and improve interactions with the borough's 270,000 residents. The initiative further solidifies 8x8's presence in the UK public sector, with XCaaS now used in over one-third of London's boroughs.

title: When Pentest Tools Go Brutal: Red-Teaming Tool Being Abused by Malicious Actors
summary: Palo Alto Networks' Unit 42 has identified that Brute Ratel C4 (BRc4), a red-teaming and adversarial attack simulation tool designed to evade EDR and AV detection, is being actively abused by malicious actors, including techniques consistent with APT29. The tool's effectiveness was highlighted by a sample that received benign verdicts from all 56 VirusTotal vendors despite containing a malicious payload. The report details the technical analysis of how BRc4 is deployed, including DLL search order hijacking and process injection, and provides indicators of compromise to help organizations detect and protect against this evolving threat.

title: What's the Impact of the Strong Dollar on My Portfolio?
summary: The strong U.S. dollar, experiencing its biggest rally in 20 years, negatively impacts non-U.S. fund returns and profitability for American companies operating overseas. While it offers advantages for consumers traveling abroad, investors in international stocks and bonds face challenges due to unfavorable exchange rates and increased repayment costs for dollar-denominated debt. Despite the difficulties, some Morningstar analysts suggest currency hedging can minimize volatility, and others view the current currency weakness as an attractive buying opportunity for international funds.

title: Big Companies Offering Employees Mid-Year Raises to Cope with Inflation
summary: Many large U.S. corporations, including Exxon Mobil Corp., PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP, Microsoft Corp., and T. Rowe Price Group Inc., are implementing mid-year raises or special bonuses for their employees to combat inflation and retain talent in a tight labor market. These moves are a response to increased living expenses and a desire to remain competitive employers, even as some executives express concerns about a potential economic slowdown. Companies are proactively adjusting compensation, with some even granting raises to new hires to address attrition and inflation pressures.

title: IBM Aims to Capture Growing Market Opportunity for Data Observability with Databand.ai Acquisition
summary: IBM has acquired Databand.ai, a data observability software provider, marking its fifth acquisition in 2022 to strengthen its hybrid cloud and AI capabilities. This acquisition aims to help enterprises address poor data quality, pipeline failures, and errors before they impact business, bolstering IBM's comprehensive observability strategy across IT operations, applications, data, and machine learning systems. The integration of Databand.ai with IBM's existing solutions like Instana APM and Watson Studio will provide a more complete view of application infrastructure and data platforms, ensuring trustworthy data for critical business processes.

title: N-able Acquires Spinpanel to Accelerate Cloud Strategy
summary: N-able, Inc. (NYSE: NABL) has acquired Spinpanel, a multi-tenant Microsoft 365 management and automation platform. This acquisition aims to help N-able partners address the challenges of labor scarcity and the shift to cloud services, particularly in managing Microsoft Cloud offerings. Spinpanel's technology will be integrated into N-able's product portfolio during the third quarter, providing partners and customers with enhanced tools for optimizing their Microsoft Cloud products and accessing a broader range of IT management and security solutions.

title: Qualys Launches VMDR 2.0 with TruRisk™ Scores and Automated Remediation Workflows
summary: Qualys (NASDAQ: QLYS) has launched VMDR 2.0 with TruRisk™ scores and automated remediation workflows, aiming to provide organizations with clearer insights into their risk posture. This new cloud-based solution helps security and IT teams prioritize and respond to critical threats more efficiently by integrating risk-based vulnerability management, correlating vulnerabilities with business criticality, and automating remediation processes through drag-and-drop workflows. Beta customers reportedly reduced critical vulnerabilities by 28% and risk by an average of 23%.

title: Understanding the liquid workforce
summary: The "liquid workforce" is a modern work model adapting to employee and business needs, driven by digitalization, mobility, and flexibility. Coined from sociologist Zygmunt Bauman's "liquid modernity," it emphasizes talent, efficiency, and work-life balance over traditional fixed hours and locations. To thrive in this environment, individuals need strong digital skills and the ability to adapt through continuous learning.

title: Amazon and Microsoft deny using Flickr pics for facial recognition, as suits test limits of privacy law
summary: Amazon and Microsoft are facing lawsuits alleging they violated the Illinois Biometric Information Privacy Act by using Flickr photos for facial recognition development without consent. Both companies deny using the IBM "Diversity in Faces" database for their AI algorithms after initial downloads. The cases highlight broader issues concerning the lack of a national privacy law, the trade-offs between privacy and AI accuracy, and jurisdictional complexities in the cloud era.

title: Why Adobe Stock Is Down 35% So Far in 2022
summary: Adobe's stock has dropped 35% in the first half of 2022 due to a slowing growth pace, despite strong sales and cash flow. Investors are concerned about a "growth hangover" as work patterns normalize post-pandemic, leading to a conservative outlook from management for the latter half of the year. While the company still expects strong sales for 2022, the short-term market focus on decelerating demand is pressuring the stock.

title: FMET Makes It Simple to Take Long View of Metaverse
summary: The Fidelity Metaverse ETF (FMET) offers investors a way to engage with the growing metaverse theme, which is projected to be worth over $800 million by 2028. Despite a retrenchment in growth stocks, the long-term outlook for the metaverse remains compelling, especially with established companies like Meta Platforms, Alphabet, Apple, and Nvidia investing heavily in its development. FMET provides a diversified basket approach to this theme, including exposure to gaming and numerous mega-cap growth companies, with an affordable annual fee.

title: Fujitsu acquires ServiceNow partner Enable
summary: Fujitsu Australia has acquired Melbourne-based ServiceNow partner Enable Professional Services, marking its third acquisition in 15 months. This deal will grant Fujitsu access to Enable's ServiceNow advisory, consulting, and delivery services, along with its employees across multiple Asian countries. The acquisition aims to bolster Fujitsu's business applications focus under its new global Uvance brand, with Enable operating as a stand-alone Fujitsu company.

title: Gurus foresee 'virtual humans' enhancing many industries
summary: Experts predict that virtual humans, fueled by AI advancements, will revolutionize various industries such as retail, finance, and education. Production costs and development times for digital avatars are expected to decrease significantly, leading to widespread adoption. Companies like Baidu are already investing heavily in this technology, with the market in China projected to reach 10.24 billion yuan ($1.5 billion) by 2026.

title: In a Tough Quarter, Sustainable Strategies Struggled But Stayed Competitive
summary: In the second quarter, sustainable investing strategies faced headwinds as technology stocks, prominent in many ESG portfolios, declined, and energy stocks, often excluded, performed strongly. Despite this, many sustainable equity strategies, particularly those leveraging healthcare and consumer staples, managed to stay competitive and, in some cases, even outperformed the broader market. Over the long term, ESG-focused strategies continue to show strong performance relative to the market, indicating resilience despite short-term market shifts.

title: HPE exec: GreenLake is to HPE as AWS is to Amazon
summary: Omer Asad, VP and GM at HPE, explains that GreenLake is central to HPE's transformation into a platform company, akin to how AWS functions for Amazon or Azure for Microsoft. GreenLake offers customers a cloud-like consumption experience for infrastructure, moving away from traditional hardware sales to a service-based model. This shift addresses customer desires for simplified infrastructure consumption and outcome-based solutions rather than focusing on raw hardware specifications.

title: Payment solutions for fuel providers
summary: J.P. Morgan's article addresses the evolving challenges and opportunities for fuel providers in the payments landscape. It highlights the complexities of managing multiple payment systems in fuel retail, the financial burden of swipe fees and fraud, and the need for modernization. The article suggests that adopting new payment models, leveraging mobile apps, and offering diversified services like EV charging can help fuel retailers attract and retain customers and optimize operational costs.

title: NetApp Ontap to be sole vSAN storage alternative in the cloud
summary: NetApp's Ontap-based cloud storage services will become the exclusive vSAN storage alternative officially supported by VMware's vSphere instances in the cloud. This partnership allows enterprise customers to extend VMware data stores in AWS, Azure, and Google clouds using Ontap as an external NFS data store, offering a more cost-effective solution than traditional vSAN. The move aims to provide a familiar and integrated storage experience for VMware customers migrating to the cloud.

title: Citrix-Tibco New CEO Tom Krause: 5 Huge Things To Know
summary: Tom Krause is leaving his key role at Broadcom, where he was the public face of the VMware acquisition, to become the new CEO of the combined Citrix Systems and Tibco Software. His departure is significant as he was slated to lead VMware post-merger, and he will now compete directly with Broadcom-VMware in the software market. Private equity firms Vista Equity Partners and Elliott Investment Management, who are acquiring Citrix and merging it with Tibco, express high confidence in Krause's extensive industry experience to lead the new entity.

title: Walmart Is Weaning Itself Off of Big Tech
summary: Walmart is developing its own cloud infrastructure to reduce its reliance on major tech companies like Microsoft Azure and Google Cloud. This strategic move aims to bring its data management and operational technology in-house. The article highlights Walmart's efforts to create its own internal cloud services for its extensive operations.

title: WaterNSW lays the foundation for HR automation using robust technology
summary: WaterNSW, a state-owned corporation, has implemented Microsoft Dynamics 365 Human Resources as a core component of its digital transformation, aiming to automate HR processes and enhance employee experience. This initiative, part of a three-horizon strategy, focuses on simplifying HR operations, improving data management, and providing self-service capabilities for its 1,000 employees. The transition to an agile delivery model allowed for rapid development and optimization of the HR case management platform, leading to better reporting and cost efficiencies.

title: FlexShares Slashes Fees on U.S. Quality Large-Cap ETF
summary: FlexShares has reduced the expense ratio for its US Quality Large Cap Index Fund (QLC B) from 0.32% to 0.25%, effective July 11, 2202. This move positions QLC among the least expensive offerings in its category, aiming to boost demand amidst market volatility. The fund tracks the Northern Trust Quality Large Cap Index, focusing on quality metrics for large-cap U.S. companies.

title: Netflix names Microsoft as partner for ad-supported subscription plan
summary: Netflix has selected Microsoft as its technology and sales partner for its upcoming ad-supported subscription plan. This move comes as Netflix seeks to boost subscriber growth after experiencing losses, aligning with other streaming services that offer ad-supported tiers. Microsoft's strong advertising revenue and recent acquisition of Xandr Inc. make it a suitable partner, with Netflix's Chief Operating Officer emphasizing increased consumer choice and a premium advertiser experience.

title: Netflix Partners With Microsoft for New Advertising-Backed Option
summary: Netflix has selected Microsoft to be its technology and sales partner for its new lower-cost, advertising-backed subscription plan. This partnership aims to boost Netflix's revenue and subscription growth after the company reported its first subscriber loss in over a decade in the March quarter. The move also significantly benefits Microsoft's expanding advertising business.

title: Managing User Identity in a Cloud-First World
summary: In a cloud-first world with increased remote work, traditional security tools struggle to establish Zero Trust due to fragmented user identities across various cloud and on-premise providers. This article introduces Palo Alto Networks' enhanced Cloud Identity Engine, integrated with PAN-OS 10.2, designed to simplify identity-based security controls, unify identity across infrastructure, and improve visibility for consistent Zero Trust implementation.

title: Read the Charter Issue of PC Magazine From 1982
summary: This article looks back at the charter issue of PC Magazine from 1982, discussing its founding by David Bunnell and the early challenges in its creation and growth. It highlights the magazine's journey from print to digital, its initial success, and the eventual sale to Ziff-Davis, which led to the founding of a rival, PC World. The article also details some of the content from the inaugural issue, including an interview with Bill Gates.

title: Twelve and Alaska Airlines to collaborate with Microsoft to advance sustainable aviation fuel derived from recaptured CO2 and renewable energy
summary: Twelve, Alaska Airlines, and Microsoft have partnered to advance sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) derived from recaptured CO2 and renewable energy. The collaboration aims to develop and demonstrate Twelve's E-Jet®, a low-carbon jet fuel, with the ultimate goal of powering commercial flights and reducing the aviation industry's reliance on fossil fuels. This initiative supports Alaska Airlines' path to net-zero emissions by 2040 and Microsoft's efforts to decarbonize hard-to-abate sectors.

title: Tom Linebarger to step down as Cummins CEO, remain chairman
summary: Tom Linebarger will step down as CEO of Cummins Inc. on August 1st, 2022, after leading the engine manufacturing company since 2012. He will remain as chairman of the board and in an executive chairman role. Jennifer Rumsey, currently Cummins President and Chief Operating Officer, will succeed him, becoming the company's seventh CEO and the first woman to hold the position.

title: Prime Day 2022 was the biggest Prime Day event ever
summary: Prime Day 2022 proved to be the largest Prime Day event in Amazon's history, with members purchasing over 300 million items worldwide and saving more than $1.7 billion. This year also marked the biggest Prime Day for Amazon's small and medium-sized selling partners, whose sales growth outpaced Amazon's retail business. Customers spent over $3 billion on small business items, highlighting a significant focus on supporting these businesses during the event.

title: Microsoft Inspire 2022: Empowering partners to drive transformation in every industry
summary: Microsoft Inspire 2022 is focused on empowering partners to drive digital transformation across various industries by leveraging the Microsoft Cloud. The company is offering four key value propositions—Build, Enrich, Unlock, and Scale—to help partners develop innovative solutions and address customer needs. The event features key speakers and sessions covering industry clouds, sustainability, and opportunities in healthcare, financial services, retail, manufacturing, and other sectors.

title: Chip Shortage Turns into Surplus
summary: The global chip shortage, exacerbated by the coronavirus pandemic and high demand for electronics, has unexpectedly turned into a surplus due to high inflation, China's COVID restrictions, and the war in Ukraine, which reduced consumer spending. This shift has severely impacted semiconductor stocks, with companies like Micron Technology reducing production and manufacturers, especially in computing and smartphones, now facing an oversupply. The situation is worsened by hoarding practices, though some sectors like Apple suppliers and, for now, automobile chipmakers, are less affected.

title: Tech Moves: Vimeo hires Seattle execs; Microsoft corporate VP retires; and more
summary: Vimeo has appointed Lynn Girotto as chief marketing officer and Ashraf Alkarmi as chief product officer, both based in the Seattle area. Microsoft corporate vice president Sam George is retiring after 25 years with the company. The article also details new hires at Absci, Amazon, SeekOut, RealNetworks, and TEAL, covering key personnel changes in the Pacific Northwest tech community.

title: Netflix, Microsoft And The Rapidly Blurring Lines Between Media And Tech
summary: The article discusses the increasing convergence of media and technology industries, highlighted by Netflix's partnership with Microsoft for its ad-supported tier and Disney's ad tech collaboration with The Trade Desk. It also points to Apple TV+'s exclusive streaming deal for Major League Soccer as another example of tech companies making significant moves into content. The author uses the metaphor of Certs mints to illustrate how Netflix and Microsoft are becoming "two industries in one," emphasizing the blurring lines between these sectors.

title: +25년간 쉼없이 배당준 배당귀족주 ETF ; NOBL ETF 투자에 대해 공부해보기
summary: This article discusses investing in the NOBL ETF, which focuses on Dividend Aristocrats—S&P 500 companies that have consistently increased dividends for at least 25 years. It explains the NOBL ETF's characteristics, including its investment strategy, current portfolio of 64 companies, and expense ratio, while noting its exclusion of major tech stocks like Apple and Microsoft. The author suggests it as a "peace-of-mind" investment during volatile market conditions.

title: Spectralink DECT handsets Microsoft Teams now supported with Teams SIP Gateway
summary: Spectralink DECT handsets are now officially certified and supported for Microsoft Teams via the Teams SIP Gateway, making Spectralink the first vendor to achieve this. This development allows organizations, particularly those in retail and manufacturing, to integrate DECT solutions directly with Teams Phone, removing the need for traditional PBXs or SBCs. The article details the architecture, benefits, and how to acquire Spectralink DECT solutions for Teams, highlighting their rugged design and specialized features suitable for various work environments.

title: Reddit Turns One Down Under
summary: Reddit is celebrating its one-year anniversary of expanding into Australia, which is now its fourth-largest user base. To commemorate this milestone, Reddit is launching its inaugural Australian consumer brand campaign, "Find your people," highlighting its diverse communities and increasing engagement with Australian users and brands. The platform has seen significant growth in local teams and user activity across various communities, including a successful partnership with the Australian Football League and effective ad campaigns for brands like Up.

title: Microsoft wants to add Stories to company intranets
summary: Microsoft is introducing a "Stories" feature to its Viva "employee experience" platform, called Viva Engage, aiming to bring the popular snackable content format to corporate intranets. This new AI-powered component for Microsoft Teams will allow employees to create and share video Stories, serving as a replacement for Yammer Communities for Teams. While questions remain about its adoption given past intranet engagement issues, Microsoft believes Stories can foster connections and cater to a workforce familiar with such modalities from personal social platforms.

title: LinkedIn Still Number One Brand to be Faked in Phishing Attempts while Microsoft Surges up the Rankings to Number Two Spot in Q2 Report
summary: Check Point Research's Q2 Brand Phishing Report reveals that LinkedIn remains the most imitated brand in phishing attempts, accounting for 45% of all such attacks. Microsoft has significantly risen to the second spot with 13%, surpassing DHL, while new brands like Adidas, Adobe, and HSBC have entered the top 10. The report highlights the dangers of these scams, with examples provided for LinkedIn, DHL, Outlook, and Amazon phishing attempts.

title: Carolyn Everson Re-Emerges With a Seat on Coca-Cola Board
summary: Carolyn Everson, a former executive at Facebook, Microsoft, and Instacart, has been elected to The Coca-Cola Company's Board of Directors. Everson, who left Instacart at the end of last year, already serves on the board of talent agency CAA and has been working as an advisor and agency investor. Her appointment adds significant digital and tech experience to Coca-Cola's board.

title: Microsoft training AI in drones
summary: Microsoft is developing Project AirSim, a flight simulator for autonomous aircraft to train AI systems for drones in a virtual environment. This platform allows companies to test drone software in risky scenarios and adverse conditions, significantly reducing development time. The project, running on Azure, aims to provide a safe space for companies like Airtonomy to develop and test crucial flight routines for infrastructure inspection, and eventually offer a free option and pre-trained AI "building blocks."

title: Netflix loses nearly 1 million subscribers, but helped by ‘Stranger Things’
summary: Netflix reported a loss of 970,000 subscribers in the second quarter, yet this was less than their forecast of 2 million, largely thanks to the popularity of "Stranger Things." To combat subscriber declines and increased competition, Netflix plans to introduce a cheaper, ad-supported plan in partnership with Microsoft and is cracking down on password sharing. Despite the losses and stock plunge, Netflix remains a dominant streaming force, albeit with slower growth projections for the upcoming quarter.

title: Microsoft Cloud for Sovereignty: The most flexible and comprehensive solution for digital sovereignty
summary: Microsoft Cloud for Sovereignty is a new solution enabling public sector customers to use Microsoft Cloud while meeting compliance, security, and policy needs, including data residency and sovereign controls. It provides increased control over data and transparency into cloud operations and governance processes. The solution is partner-led and focuses on working with in-country partners to deliver customized cloud solutions that address unique government requirements.

title: Top 10 manufacturers using digital twins
summary: This article lists the top 10 manufacturers leveraging digital twin technology to enhance efficiency, sustainability, and problem-solving in their operations. Companies like Microsoft, IBM, Oracle, Siemens, and GE are using virtual models to optimize various aspects of manufacturing, from product design and performance prediction to supply chain management and IoT device integration. The adoption of digital twins helps these industry leaders to drive innovation, reduce costs, and address complex challenges in a connected world.

title: AiThority Interview with Julie Lock, Senior Manager, UK&I Marketing at HubSpot
summary: Julie Lock, Senior Manager, UK&I Marketing at HubSpot, discusses her role, HubSpot's customer-centric approach, and the evolution of CRMs. She highlights how HubSpot's platform differs from competitors and addresses key challenges CRMs solve for different departments. Lock also shares insights on the integration of AI with CRMs, the relationship between CRMs and CDPs, and market differences between the UK and North America, all while emphasizing the importance of solving for the customer in a strong economic climate.

title: KKR Acquires Atlantic Yards Office Property Leased to Microsoft in Atlanta
summary: KKR has acquired Atlantic Yards, a 523,511-square-foot, two-building office property in Midtown Atlanta, which is fully leased to Microsoft Corp. The property, built in 2021 within the Atlantic Station mixed-use development, was sold by a joint venture between Hines and Invesco Real Estate. Microsoft's lease extends through 2035, with the facility expected to house 1,500 to 2,000 employees focused on AI and cloud-based services.

title: SnapMirror in the Cloud: New Uses for NetApp Data Replication
summary: NetApp's SnapMirror, a long-standing enterprise data replication solution, is now extended to the cloud through Cloud Volumes ONTAP. This integration opens up new use cases for SnapMirror, including cloud-based disaster recovery, efficient cloud migration, application development and analytics, and multicloud architecture. It also plays a role in NetApp Cloud Backup, enhancing data protection and efficiency across hybrid and multicloud environments by leveraging block-level replication and storage efficiencies like deduplication and compression.

title: If AI had a voice!
summary: This article explores the inherent gender bias in Artificial Intelligence, arguing that AI often reflects and amplifies the biases of its creators. Through examples like language translation and common AI voice assistants, the author demonstrates how AI frequently defaults to male coding for leadership roles and female for assistive roles, mirroring societal stereotypes. While acknowledging that machine learning is evolving to address these biases, the piece emphasizes the ongoing need for greater inclusion and feedback to achieve true gender neutrality in AI development.

title: Adam & Eve signs deal with data science agency Track
summary: Adam & Eve DDB Group is expanding its customer experience and data science capabilities by forming a partnership with German Omnicom sister agency Track. This collaboration follows their initial success in winning the integrated JetBlue business in the US last year. The new integrated unit will be led by Simon Adamson, chief experience officer of Adam & Eve DDB Group, and Track managing director Phillip Schilling, aiming to scale their offering and create more meaningful customer experiences.

title: Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce – Digital Transformation Strategies
summary: This report details Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce's (CIBC) digital transformation strategies, focusing on its use of AI, cloud, blockchain, and online payments. It covers CIBC's ICT spending, technology focus areas, partnerships, investments, and initiatives to enhance its digital banking capabilities. The article also provides insights into key ICT spending categories and technology themes for the company.

title: Netflix Lost Nearly 1 Million Subscribers Last Quarter. Here’s What That Means for Its Future
summary: Netflix reported a loss of nearly 1 million subscribers in the second quarter of 2022, compounding its 200,000 subscriber loss from the previous quarter. Despite this, the total loss was less than projected, leading to a temporary stock surge, though shares remain significantly down for the year. In response, Netflix is pursuing efforts like an ad-supported tier and focusing on high-quality original content to drive future growth and revenue.

title: First Lady of Ukraine Accepts Computer Donation from HP Inc. for Ukrainian Children and Healthcare Workers
summary: First Lady of Ukraine, Olena Zelenska, met with HP Inc. and the Global Business Coalition for Education to accept a donation of technology and learning materials for Ukrainian children and healthcare workers. This initiative, "Digital Equity for Ukraine," is a $30 million partnership aimed at providing computers to displaced students and families, with Microsoft offering software support. The computers will be distributed both within Ukraine and to refugees outside the country to ensure continued learning and support during the ongoing conflict.

title: Oracle and Microsoft announce availability of Oracle Database Service for Microsoft Azure
summary: Oracle and Microsoft have announced the general availability of Oracle Database Service for Microsoft Azure, enabling Azure customers to easily provision, access, and monitor Oracle Database services on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI). This collaboration extends their 2019 partnership on Oracle Interconnect for Microsoft Azure, simplifying multicloud operations for joint customers. The service bears no charges for usage, data egress/ingress between OCI and Azure, with customers only paying for consumed Azure or Oracle services.

title: Oracle and Microsoft Agree to Deepen Interoperability of Cloud Platforms
summary: Oracle Corp. and Microsoft Corp. have announced a deeper interoperability between their cloud platforms, enabling customers to more easily run projects across both services. This agreement reflects an evolving market where customers utilize multiple clouds and resist being locked into a single provider. The move acknowledges the multicloud environment, with about two-thirds of enterprise-level companies already using multiple cloud solutions.

title: FaZe Clan Has Gone Public
summary: Gaming and lifestyle media platform FaZe Clan has officially gone public, completing a business combination with B. Riley Principal 150 Merger Corp. Shares began trading under "FAZE" and "FAZEW" at a $725 million valuation. With this move, FaZe Clan aims to access capital for growth and allow fans to own part of its future, leveraging its influence among Gen Z.

title: News | KKR Closes on the Highest-Priced Atlanta Office Building Deal of Past Year
summary: Private equity firm KKR has acquired two office buildings in Atlanta, fully leased by Microsoft, for $385 million. This transaction represents the highest-priced office building deal in Atlanta over the past year. The article notes that this content is exclusively available to CoStar subscribers.

title: Microsoft Teams back up for most users after global outage
summary: Microsoft Teams, used by over 270 million people globally, experienced an hours-long outage that disrupted services for tens of thousands of users worldwide. Microsoft attributed the disruption to a broken connection in a recent software update and confirmed that the service was largely restored. The company is actively monitoring for any lasting impacts and ensuring full recovery of all functions.

title: Why is American Express paying people to play Halo 4?
summary: American Express is offering financial incentives to Halo 4 players by syncing their Xbox accounts with their Amex cards. Players can receive $10 for syncing and an additional $25 for reaching a specific game milestone, allowing them to recoup a portion of the game's cost. This strategy aims to reduce cardholder attrition and attract new customers from the growing video game market, according to industry experts.

title: Korean DL E&C to enter SMR biz with Canada’s Terrestrial
summary: DL E&C, a South Korean construction company, is entering the small modular reactor (SMR) business through a partnership with Canadian firm Terrestrial Energy Inc. Their collaboration focuses on developing and deploying Terrestrial's integral molten salt reactor (IMSR) cogeneration plants, particularly for industrial applications in the chemical and petrochemical sectors. DL E&C aims to leverage its expertise in plant development to commercialize IMSR technology by 2031, providing carbon-free power and thermal energy.

title: Top Software Trends for Financial Advisors
summary: This article analyzes the key findings of the T3/Inside Information Technology Survey, providing insights into the software used by financial advisors and emerging technology trends. It highlights the widespread adoption of CRM and financial planning software, while also pointing out surprising gaps in the use of portfolio management, account aggregation, and cybersecurity tools. The author emphasizes the importance for advisors to leverage technology to provide comprehensive services and remain competitive.

title: Will Facebook-like features in Viva Engage help build corporate culture?
summary: Microsoft's new Viva Engage, based on Yammer, features a Facebook-like interface with "storylines" for text, images, and video, aiming to foster corporate culture in hybrid work environments. Industry analysts believe these "non-work" communication features can create a "virtual watercooler" effect, improving employee experience, belonging, and overall wellbeing. The integration of consumer-grade social media features into enterprise tools like Teams is seen as a way to boost adoption and offer a competitive edge in the HCM market.

title: Microsoft Teams back up for most users after global outage
summary: Microsoft Teams has largely recovered from a global outage that affected tens of thousands of users. The disruption was attributed to a recent software update containing a broken connection to an internal storage service. The company is monitoring for any residual impact and ensuring all functions are fully restored.

title: Microsoft Opposes Summary Judgment for IRS in FOIA Suit
summary: Microsoft has filed an opposition to the IRS's motion for summary judgment in a Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) lawsuit, arguing that the IRS's search for responsive documents was inadequate. Microsoft asserts that the IRS failed to search for relevant records created by its contractors, Boies Schiller Flexner LLP and Quinn Emanuel Urquhart & Sullivan, LLP, and that the IRS's justifications for withholding documents are legally insufficient. The company contends that its contracts with these firms define contractor-generated work as IRS agency records and that the IRS exercised extensive control over these records.

title: Oracle adds new chapter for multicloud story through cloud database service with Microsoft
summary: Oracle and Microsoft have announced the availability of Oracle Database Service for Microsoft Azure, allowing Azure customers streamlined access to Oracle Database Services on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI). This partnership aims to simplify multicloud solutions for their shared enterprise customer base, building on a previous interoperability alliance from 2019. The new service enables Azure users to provision and monitor Oracle Database Services in OCI and build applications on Azure that connect to Oracle services such as Autonomous Database.

title: Enter Microsoft Viva Engage. A Real Social Network For The Enterprise?
summary: Microsoft has launched Viva Engage, a new application within Microsoft Viva, which is described as an "Instagram for the enterprise." This platform aims to provide a dedicated space for personal connections, employee belonging, and social interactions at work, separate from work-oriented collaboration tools like Slack or Microsoft Teams. The author argues that such platforms, which allow employees to share personal interests and engage in non-work-related discussions, can significantly benefit companies by fostering a stronger sense of belonging and making work more engaging.

title: Best Flash Drives: Kingston DataTraveler Max & Sandisk Extreme Pro
summary: This article reviews and compares eight USB 3.2 flash drives from top brands like Kingston, Sandisk, Lexar, Samsung, and Corsair, focusing on performance, design, and build quality. The Kingston DataTraveler Max is highlighted as the best overall for its speed and value, while alternatives like the Sandisk Extreme Pro and Lexar JumpDrive M900 are recommended for specific needs. The article also provides detailed benchmark analysis for movie and photo transfer speeds, as well as insights into throttling issues and physical durability.

title: CDHU Enhances Citizen Services by Leveraging the Cloud
summary: The Housing and Urban Development Company (CDHU) of São Paulo has adopted Microsoft's cloud technologies, including Dynamics 365, Power Apps, and Microsoft 365, to centralize its CRM processes and enhance citizen services. This digital transformation has created a robust customer service channel, improved data management, streamlined housing financing registrations, and enabled field teams to conduct diagnoses more efficiently. The initiative has significantly boosted agility, reduced manual work, and standardized services for the population.

title: What’s New in NVIDIA AI Enterprise 2.1 | NVIDIA Technical Blog
summary: NVIDIA AI Enterprise 2.1 is now generally available, offering an optimized and supported software suite for deploying and scaling AI applications across various environments. Key updates include advanced data science capabilities with NVIDIA RAPIDS 22.04, low-code AI model development using NVIDIA TAO Toolkit 22.05 with new features like REST APIs and pre-trained models, and expanded public cloud support for Red Hat OpenShift and Microsoft Azure NVads A10 v5 series. These enhancements enable affordable GPU sharing, optimized performance for deep learning inferencing, and flexibility for enterprises in managing AI infrastructure.

title: Top stock reports to watch this week (25.07.2022)
summary: The article highlights the key earnings reports scheduled for the week of July 25, 2022, focusing on major US tech companies like Alphabet, Microsoft, Meta Platforms, Amazon, and Apple. It notes that the Wall Street earnings season is in full swing, with several Dow Jones members also reporting their financial results. This week is expected to be significant for traders due to the high-profile companies announcing their earnings.

title: Healthcare Triangle launches regional HQ in Singapore to bolster medical innovation in APAC
summary: Healthcare Triangle Inc. has inaugurated its regional headquarters in Singapore, planning to invest $25 million to advance digital healthcare across the Asia Pacific region. This expansion aims to foster medical innovation, create over 500 jobs, and support the digital transformation of healthcare and pharmaceutical sectors by leveraging cloud-based platforms. The company's focus includes strategic partnerships and collaborations to build a more resilient healthcare ecosystem in the APAC region.

title: ServiceNow Inc. stock falls Monday, underperforms market
summary: ServiceNow Inc. stock saw a 1.52% decline on Monday, closing at $440.00, despite an overall positive trading session for the stock market. This marks the second consecutive day of losses for the company, which is $267.60 short of its 52-week high. ServiceNow also underperformed against competitors like Microsoft and Qualcomm, although it did better than International Business Machines Corp.

title: iRhythm Gains FDA Clearance for its Clinically Integrated ZEUS System
summary: iRhythm Technologies announced FDA 510(k) clearance for its ZEUS System for the Zio Watch, developed in partnership with Verily. This integrated solution provides a clinical-grade, wrist-worn wearable for long-term continuous monitoring to detect and characterize atrial fibrillation (AFib), aiding clinicians in diagnosis and intervention. The Zio Watch with the ZEUS System aims to enhance patient care by offering a cost-effective and noninvasive monitoring platform, leveraging iRhythm's extensive ECG data repository and proprietary AI algorithms.

title: Apple's earnings will give a peek into the mindset of the high-end consumer
summary: Apple is set to report its third-quarter earnings, which analysts and investors will closely scrutinize for insights into the impact of macroeconomic trends like inflation and rising interest rates on high-end consumer spending. While Apple's sales have historically been robust due to its affluent customer base, any indication of slowing demand for iPhones and Macs could signal broader economic concerns. The company's performance will also reflect its ability to manage supply chain issues and COVID-19 lockdowns in China, as well as the growth trajectory of its services business.

title: Check Point Research: Weekly Cyber Attacks increased by 32% Year-Over-Year; 1 out of 40 organizations impacted by Ransomware
summary: Check Point Research reports a 32% year-over-year increase in global cyber-attacks in Q2 2022, with the average weekly attacks per organization reaching 1.2K. The Education/Research sector remains the most targeted, experiencing a 53% increase in attacks. Ransomware attacks have seen a 59% global increase, impacting 1 out of 40 organizations weekly, with the Retail/Wholesale sector seeing a dramatic 182% surge.

title: Tencent tops Apple, Sony to take gaming market crown
summary: Tencent Holdings has overtaken industry giants like Sony and Apple to become the leading company in the gaming market, primarily through over 180 strategic, smaller investments worldwide. Despite regulatory challenges in China and increased competition from large acquisitions by Microsoft and Sony, Tencent is intensifying its focus on overseas markets, planning a global release for its top game "Honor of Kings," as its value-added services segment remains highly profitable. The Chinese tech giant's diverse global portfolio has allowed it to achieve significant revenue figures even as it navigates a changing domestic and international landscape.

title: From burgers to hi-tech gadgets, stressed consumers buy cheap
summary: Global consumers are showing mixed signals due to record inflation, with lower-income households sticking to essential goods and cheaper options, while wealthier consumers continue to splurge on luxury items and travel. Companies like Walmart, McDonald's, Coca-Cola, and Unilever are seeing varying impacts, with some raising prices successfully and others considering more discount options to cater to stressed consumers. The market reflects a divide, highlighting economic strain on some segments while others remain resilient in their spending habits.

title: Manufacturing Titan 3M Is Spinning Off Its Healthcare Business Into A Separate Company
summary: 3M announced its plan to spin off its healthcare division into a separate, publicly traded company. This new healthcare entity, with approximately $8.6 billion in sales in 2021, will focus on innovation in areas like wound care, oral care, healthcare IT, and biopharma filtration. The move aims to create two well-capitalized companies better positioned to pursue their respective growth strategies.

title: Lumen advances 5G technology with a simplified, holistic cybersecurity mindset
summary: Lumen embraced a simplified, holistic cybersecurity mindset to advance its 5G technology, partnering with Microsoft to address identity and compliance challenges during its cloud migration and system modernization. By implementing Azure Active Directory and other Microsoft Security solutions, Lumen has enhanced data protection, streamlined operations, and achieved greater transparency and automation in managing data access. This strategic move allows Lumen to focus on innovation while ensuring robust security and compliance for its cutting-edge 5G infrastructure.

title: Rumors of Oracle Layoffs Highlight Company's Position in Cloud Race
summary: Rumors are circulating about potential Oracle layoffs affecting thousands of workers across multiple divisions, following reports from The Information and CRN. This comes as Oracle intensifies its efforts to compete in the cloud market against giants like AWS, Microsoft Azure, and Google Cloud, despite facing an uphill battle in developer preference. While Oracle has secured wins like TikTok as a cloud client and offers competitive salaries for in-demand tech roles, its broad transformation to keep pace in the rapidly evolving cloud landscape is under scrutiny amid tech industry hiring slowdowns.

title: Piramal’s NBFC plan, Inflation bites Colgate & more
summary: Indian markets closed higher, snapping a two-day losing streak, with 46 of Nifty50 stocks in the green. Key corporate news included Piramal Enterprises receiving RBI's nod for an NBFC, Colgate-Palmolive seeing profit drops due to inflation, and Shoppers Stop reporting strong Q1 earnings. The IMF lowered India's growth forecast, while Microsoft and Alphabet missed analyst estimates.

title: Threat Brief: Microsoft Critical Vulnerabilities (CVE-2022-26809, CVE-2022-26923, CVE-2022-26925)
summary: This threat brief details three critical Microsoft vulnerabilities: CVE-2022-26809 (RPC Remote Code Execution), CVE-2022-26923 (Active Directory Privilege Escalation), and CVE-2022-26925 (Windows LSA Spoofing). Microsoft released patches in April and May 2022, and organizations are strongly advised to apply these updates as CVE-2022-26925 has been exploited in the wild. Palo Alto Networks customers receive protection through their Next-Generation Firewall and Cortex XDR.

title: Internet speed test firm Ookla acquires Swedish company CellRebel
summary: Ookla, a Seattle-based internet speed test company, has acquired Swedish firm CellRebel. This acquisition follows Ookla's earlier purchase of RootMetrics in December, indicating a strategic expansion to better understand consumer network experiences. Doug Suttles, Ookla's CEO, emphasized the need to gain deeper insights into user interactions with networks.

title: Seagate Technology Holdings PLC stock rises Wednesday, outperforms market
summary: Seagate Technology Holdings PLC (STX) saw its stock rise 3.54% on Wednesday, outperforming the broader market which also had a strong day. Despite the rise, the stock remains $38.99 short of its 52-week high. Seagate's performance was mixed compared to competitors like Microsoft Corp. and Western Digital Corp., but its trading volume surpassed its 50-day average.

title: How a Top T. Rowe Price Manager Is Positioned for a Continued Bear Market
summary: Justin White, manager of the T. Rowe Price All-Cap Opportunities Fund, is preparing his portfolio for a prolonged bear market by focusing on inflation- and recession-resistant stocks like Visa, Chubb, Veeva Systems, and Moderna. While he believes much of the market pain has already occurred, he anticipates further challenges, particularly given uncertainties surrounding a potential recession and the Federal Reserve's battle against inflation. White emphasizes individual stock selection over broad sector trends and has adjusted his portfolio by trimming growth stocks and increasing positions in more resilient companies.

title: Multi Echelon Inventory Optimization Market Analysis by Size,
summary: This report provides a detailed analysis of the global Multi Echelon Inventory Optimization (MEIO) market, covering its size, demand, future trends, challenges, and growth opportunities with forecasts up to 2030. It includes competitive analysis of key players like ToolsGroup and Manhattan Associates, segmentation by type (Software, Services) and application (Consumer Goods, Chemical, Retail, Manufacturing), and regional market breakdown. The study aims to offer insights into market dynamics, segmentation, and strategies for businesses and investors.

title: ATN International to buy Sacred Wind, but stays mum on possible sale
summary: ATN International is set to acquire Sacred Wind Enterprises for approximately $25 million in cash and $32 million in debt, making Sacred Wind the largest privately owned broadband company in New Mexico. Despite this acquisition, ATN has declined to comment on reports suggesting it has hired Goldman Sachs to explore a potential sale of the company. Financial analysts indicate the company remains stable and is pursuing investment objectives, particularly in fiber networks and cell towers, in areas eligible for US government subsidies.

title: KT ups ante with $1.5 billion spending on public sector cloud service
summary: KT Cloud Corp., a subsidiary of South Korea's telecom giant KT Corp., plans to invest up to 2 trillion won ($1.5 billion) over the next three years to expand its presence in the domestic public cloud service sector and enhance its internet data center (IDC) capacity. This move comes as competition intensifies in the Korean cloud market, with local rivals like Naver Cloud and NHN Cloud also aggressively expanding, and foreign players such as Snowflake, Amazon's AWS, Microsoft Azure, and Google Cloud Platform dominating the broader market. However, local companies are seen to have an advantage in the public sector due to meeting specific government security requirements.

title: Lessons from Target’s cloud journey, a decade in the making
summary: Target embarked on its cloud journey a decade ago, moving beyond a simple "lift and shift" to a hybrid multicloud architecture supported by Google Cloud Platform and Microsoft Azure. The retailer modernized its application stack with a microservices approach and open-source tools, overcoming initial cost challenges through significant investment in engineering and FinOps. Target plans to continue its hybrid strategy, leveraging public cloud for scalability and cost arbitrage, and private cloud for data-intensive and core business applications.

title: Touchstone US Large Cap Focused ETF Holdings
summary: The Touchstone US Large Cap Focused ETF (LCF) was established on July 29, 2022, concentrating its investments in large-cap equities. The ETF currently manages $64.97 million in assets across 47 holdings, focusing on US-listed large-cap stocks with sustainable competitive advantages or high barriers to entry. Top holdings include Alphabet Inc., Microsoft Corp., NVIDIA Corp., and Apple Inc.

title: Microsoft named a Leader in the 2022 Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for Robotic Process Automation
summary: Microsoft has been recognized as a Leader in the 2022 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Robotic Process Automation for the second consecutive year. This achievement underscores the significant momentum and expansion of their RPA offerings since 2019, including the integration of Power Automate for desktop into Windows and new features like hosted RPA bots and pay-as-you-go options. The company acknowledges the crucial contributions of its customers, community, and partners to the success of Power Automate.

title: Former Xbox head Peter Moore says Microsoft encouraged console wars to challenge Sony
summary: Peter Moore, former head of Xbox, revealed that Microsoft deliberately fueled the "console wars" to foster competition with Sony. He stated this rivalry ultimately benefited the gaming industry and pushed both companies to innovate, particularly highlighting how overcoming the Xbox 360's "Red Ring of Death" issue was crucial for Xbox's survival. Moore believes without this intense competition, the gaming landscape would be significantly poorer today.

title: PLDT activates trans-Pacific cable system seen to boost Philippine int’l data capacity
summary: PLDT Inc. has activated the Jupiter Cable System, a trans-Pacific cable network that will significantly boost the Philippines' international data capacity. This $136 million investment connects the Philippines to Japan and Los Angeles, tripling PLDT's international capacity to about 60 terabits per second. The system is expected to enhance internet speed and reliability for Filipinos, supporting the nation's digital economy and data-driven industries.

title: Microsoft Links Raspberry Robin USB Worm to Russian Evil Corp Hackers
summary: Microsoft has identified a potential connection between the Raspberry Robin USB-based worm and the Russian cybercrime group Evil Corp. The tech giant observed FakeUpdates malware delivered via Raspberry Robin infections, which subsequently led to actions resembling pre-ransomware behavior associated with Evil Corp (DEV-0243). While this marks the first evidence of post-exploitation activity for Raspberry Robin, the exact relationships between the involved threat actors remain unclear, according to experts.

title: How Novartis Is Finding The Path To Be A Digital Winner
summary: Novartis, a major pharmaceutical company, has faced challenges in its digital transformation despite significant investments. Initially, its efforts failed due to compartmentalized teams and a lack of business-wide integration of digital tools. However, during the Covid pandemic, pilot projects fostering collaboration between data scientists and business units, along with training front-line employees in data use, accelerated its digital progress, moving it towards becoming a digitally-enabled firm with a comprehensive AI application platform.

title: Webull Launches Expansion into Singapore
summary: Webull Corporation has officially launched its expansion into Singapore and the Asia-Pacific region. Through Webull Securities (Singapore) Pte. Ltd., residents can now trade U.S. and Hong Kong-listed equities, ETFs, options, and fractional shares with low commissions. This move follows Webull's success in the U.S. and Hong Kong, aiming to capture the growing mobile-first brokerage market in Asia-Pacific.

title: The Neocolonial Game Behind Musk-Bolsonaro Rendezvous
summary: This article criticizes Elon Musk's meeting with Brazilian President Jair Bolsonaro, framing it as a neocolonial act driven by resource acquisition and political manipulation. It highlights concerns about Musk's Starlink project in the Amazon, linking it to Brazil's nickel and lithium reserves, and questions the integrity of Bolsonaro's government in its dealings with foreign interests given its past dismantling of environmental monitoring bodies. The author suggests the collaboration serves to undermine Brazil's democratic processes and exploit its natural wealth for corporate gain.

title: Oracle reportedly implements layoffs as part of cost-cutting initiative
summary: Oracle Corp. is reportedly implementing layoffs in the San Francisco Bay Area and its customer experience software division as part of a cost-cutting initiative aiming to reduce expenses by up to $1 billion. These layoffs are expected to affect thousands of employees across the U.S., Canada, India, and Europe, aligning with previous reports from July. Despite these cuts, Oracle continues to experience growth in its cloud infrastructure and managed enterprise resource planning platforms, supported by its acquisition of Cerner Corp.

title: How Capital One improves visibility into Snowflake costs
summary: Capital One has launched Capital One Software, a new business selling its internal cloud cost management and governance tools, with its first product, Slingshot, targeting the Snowflake platform. This move allows Capital One to monetize its extensive cloud migration work and helps other enterprises manage Snowflake costs and automate governance, while also showcasing Snowflake's capabilities for highly regulated industries. Slingshot has already helped Capital One reduce Snowflake costs by 27%, improve cost per query by 45%, and save over 50,000 hours of work.

title: Microsoft shares attack surface management solutions | Microsoft Security Blog
summary: Microsoft has launched two new security products, Microsoft Defender Threat Intelligence and Microsoft Defender External Attack Surface Management, to help organizations combat increasingly sophisticated cyber threats. These solutions provide deeper context into threat actor activities, enable organizations to map their digital environments from an attacker's perspective, and identify unknown or unmanaged internet-facing resources. Additionally, Microsoft Sentinel now offers enhanced detection and response capabilities for SAP environments.

title: Cohesity names former VMware COO Sanjay Poonen as CEO
summary: Cohesity Inc., a data management provider, has appointed Sanjay Poonen, former COO of VMware Inc., as its new president and chief executive officer. Poonen replaces Cohesity founder Mohit Aron, who will transition to chief technology and product officer. This leadership change comes after Cohesity surpassed an annual revenue run rate of $300 million and boasts over 3,000 customers, including major financial institutions and Fortune 500 companies.

title: Arista Buys Pluribus Networks To Grow Cloud Networking Offering
summary: Arista Networks has acquired Pluribus Networks to enhance its Converged Cloud Fabric offering and strengthen its partnership with Ericsson. This is Arista's second acquisition in the quarter, following Untangle, as it focuses on acquiring technology and talent that align with its culture to expand its cloud networking solutions and address lower-end security and edge threat management markets. The acquisition was disclosed as Arista reported surpassing $1 billion in quarterly revenue for the first time, despite ongoing global supply chain challenges.

title: Palo Alto Networks Unit 42 Helps Customers Better Address Cybersecurity Threats Through New Managed Detection and Response Service
summary: Palo Alto Networks introduced its Unit 42 Managed Detection and Response (MDR) service to address the growing cybersecurity skills gap and increasing attack surfaces. This new service combines Cortex XDR technology with Unit 42's threat intelligence to provide 24/7 threat detection, investigation, and response. It aims to help organizations identify and respond to security threats in real-time, allowing them to focus on other security priorities.

title: Flow Security raises $10 million for data security platform
summary: Flow Security, an Israeli startup, has successfully raised $10 million in Seed funding led by Amiti. The company also launched its data security platform designed to continuously map and detect data-related risks for both data at rest and in motion. The platform helps organizations in highly-regulated markets improve their data security posture, with capabilities such as discovering data flows to external services, policy enforcement, and automatic threat modeling.

title: DXC Technology Sells Microsoft Dynamics Business Units to sa.global
summary: sa.global has acquired two Microsoft Dynamics business units, ReQlogic and Homebuilder One, from DXC Technology. This deal includes approximately 480 new clients, expanding sa.global's market reach and client portfolio. sa.global, which specializes in Microsoft Dynamics solutions, plans to invest heavily in the acquired products to maximize client value.

title: Join our Microsoft Technologies Discipline
summary: EPAM is actively recruiting for its Microsoft Technologies Discipline, seeking over 3,500 .NET engineers, solution architects, and managers across more than 55 countries. The company highlights opportunities to work on innovative SaaS/PaaS cloud solutions, build CI/CD pipelines, and develop cloud-native applications for world-class clients, emphasizing professional growth and a strong AI community. EPAM showcases several projects, including those in oil and gas, IoT, life sciences research, and finance, applying technologies like .NET, Azure, Kubernetes, and GenAI.

title: Ping Identity Acquired By Private Equity Firm Thoma Bravo -
summary: Private equity firm Thoma Bravo is acquiring enterprise identity software company Ping Identity for $2.8 billion, taking it private. This deal, expected to close in Q4 2022, follows Ping Identity's Q2 2022 financial results, which showed a revenue decrease and a larger net loss compared to the previous year. Thoma Bravo, known for its extensive cybersecurity investments including SailPoint, Proofpoint, ConnectWise, N-able, and Sophos, adds Ping Identity to its portfolio, with Vista Equity Partners supporting the acquisition.

title: Oracle Reportedly Initiating Layoffs in Bay Area, Other Locations
summary: Oracle has reportedly begun laying off thousands of employees in Silicon Valley and other global locations, targeting a billon dollars in expenses. These cuts occur despite strong profits and revenues, as Oracle is heavily investing in becoming a major cloud-services player to compete with Amazon Web Services, Microsoft Azure, and Google Cloud, while simultaneously continuing to pay specialized technologists competitive salaries. The company's strategy involves significant investment in cloud infrastructure while also reducing its workforce in other areas.

title: Semtech buys Sierra Wireless in $1.2bn deal ...
summary: Semtech has announced a definitive agreement to acquire wireless module maker Sierra Wireless for $1.2 billion, significantly expanding its market in cellular IoT modules and cloud services. The deal is expected to double Semtech's annual revenue and enhance its position in the Internet of Everything market by combining cellular, LoRa, and cloud services. This acquisition follows similar consolidation in the IoT sector and positions Semtech to offer multi-radio solutions and chip-to-cloud services.

title: Read the Charter Issue of PC Magazine From 1982
summary: PCMag celebrates its 40th anniversary by making the charter issue of PC Magazine from 1982 available for readers. The article details the magazine's origin, its founding by David Bunnell, early struggles, and eventual sale to Ziff-Davis Publishing. It highlights key content from the first issue, including an interview with Bill Gates and an evaluation of the IBM PC.

title: Salesforce Shuts Hong Kong Office Amid Brewing US - China Tensions; Consolidates Partnership With Alibaba
summary: Salesforce is closing its Hong Kong office and consolidating its strategic partnership with Alibaba Group Holding Limited to expand its software relationship management presence in Greater China. This move comes amid increasing US-China tensions and new Chinese data regulations, following other tech giants scaling back their presence. Salesforce will focus on hiring in Guangzhou, with Alibaba handling sales in mainland China and Hong Kong, and Singapore managing Taiwan.

title: Touchstone Dividend Select ETF ETF Price, Holdings, & News (NYSEARCA:DVND)
summary: The Touchstone Dividend Select ETF (DVND) focuses on generating income and capital appreciation by investing in large-cap US companies with sustainable competitive advantages, reliable dividends, and reasonable valuations. Launched on August 2, 2022, the ETF has $36.56 million in assets under management and a net expense ratio of 0.50%. Its top holdings include Dreyfus Govt Cash Mgmt-I, Microsoft, Broadcom, Johnson & Johnson, and Apple.

title: Microstrategy Outperforms Every Asset Class and Big Tech Stock Since Adopting Bitcoin Strategy, Says CEO
summary: Microstrategy CEO Michael Saylor highlights that the company's bitcoin strategy has led to significant outperformance against all asset classes and major tech stocks since its adoption. Saylor attributes this success to bitcoin's digital property characteristics and its appeal as a safe haven asset. The company's unique approach involved acquiring substantial bitcoin holdings and integrating it into their corporate strategy.

title: How the economic downturn is affecting the AI sector
summary: The economic downturn is impacting the AI sector, with enterprises cutting budgets and slowing AI projects, despite AI being an integral part of the economy. While some vendors and venture capitalists are feeling the squeeze through stricter investment processes and hiring freezes, others remain insulated due to prior budgeting or long-term investment strategies. Experts suggest experimental AI projects will be paused, but the long-term outlook for next-generation AI technologies remains positive.

title: A New Way to Connect Microsoft Teams with the Contact Centre
summary: This article discusses the growing need to integrate contact center capabilities with Microsoft Teams, especially for businesses seeking a unified platform for communications and customer service. It highlights the Voca Conversational Interaction Center by AudioCodes as a solution that offers "contact center lite" features and conversational AI, leveraging Microsoft's ecosystem. The piece also details three models for Teams contact center integrations (Connect, Extend, Power), with AudioCodes' Voca adopting the advanced "Power" model to enhance agent and customer experiences.

title: Press Release Details
summary: Bridgestone announced an expanded collaboration with Microsoft to accelerate its digital transformation and enhance its connected tires and mobility solutions globally. The partnership will leverage Microsoft Azure to integrate advanced tire analytics, benefiting global fleet and OEM customers by optimizing tire maintenance and retreading. This extended collaboration supports Bridgestone’s E8 Commitment, specifically focusing on "Efficiency," "Extension," and "Economy" values through technical innovation in AI and machine learning.

title: Nio sets up mobile technology company, first phone coming next year - ArenaEV
summary: Nio has officially established "Nio Mobile Technologies Co Ltd" with a registered capital of $100 million, signaling its entry into the smartphone market. The company aims to develop and sell electronic products, mobile devices, and wearable devices, with a self-developed phone expected next year. Nio's CEO confirmed plans for an annual phone release, designed to integrate seamlessly with Nio vehicles and offered at a competitive price compared to Apple products.

title: One Million Xbox Players Join NARAKA: BLADEPOINT in First Two Weeks of Launch
summary: Within two weeks of its launch on Xbox Series X|S and Xbox Game Pass, the battle royale game NARAKA: BLADEPOINT has attracted one million new Xbox players. Developed by NetEase and 24 Entertainment, the game is known for its fast-paced melee combat and will also be released on Xbox One before the end of 2022. Upcoming content includes a new map, Holoroth, on August 19, and the first chapter of a campaign mode for Xbox players on August 5.

title: Thoma Bravo adds Ping Identity to growing cyber security portfolio in $2.8 billion acquisition
summary: Thoma Bravo has acquired Ping Identity, a digital security specialist, for $2.8 billion, further expanding its cybersecurity portfolio which already includes Sophos and Proofpoint. The acquisition is expected to accelerate Ping Identity's cloud transformation and strengthen its position in the enterprise identity solutions market. This move highlights Thoma Bravo's continued investment in high-growth cloud software security businesses.

title: Reuters journalists in US plan first strike in decades
summary: Reuters journalists in the US are planning their first strike in decades, a 24-hour walkout, over a dispute regarding pay increases. The Communications Workers of America’s NewsGuild, representing about 300 US-based Reuters employees, states the company offered a 1% salary hike against 9% inflation and did not negotiate in good faith. The strike is timed with the company's second-quarter earnings announcement, aiming to disrupt newsgathering and draw attention to their demands.

title: Things Are Looking Bad For This World Of Warcraft Spinoff
summary: An unannounced "World of Warcraft" mobile MMO game, in development for three years by Blizzard and NetEase, has reportedly been canceled due to a financial dispute between the two companies. This cancellation follows earlier challenges for their partnership, including a crackdown on "Diablo Immortal" in China, and raises concerns about the future of the lucrative Blizzard-NetEase collaboration. Fans hoping for a true mobile "WoW" experience will have to continue waiting.

title: Gartner CFO Survey Reveals Real Estate and Finance Functions Most Likely to Face Cuts Within a Year
summary: A July 2022 Gartner survey of over 200 CFOs indicates that real estate/facilities management and finance functions are most vulnerable to budget cuts in the next year due to factors like increased remote work. Conversely, IT and sales functions are expected to see spending increases, with 40% of CFOs planning to boost IT investment, reflecting a focus on digital technology and automation to combat inflation and drive growth. The report suggests that "efficient growth" companies, which strategically invest during economic difficulties, achieve better long-term results.

title: Oracle lays off hundreds of employees
summary: Oracle has laid off hundreds of employees, primarily from its advertising and customer experience group, to prioritize its healthcare IT services and cloud businesses. This move comes after its recent $28.3 billion acquisition of Cerner Corp. and reflects a broader trend of tech companies making staffing adjustments amid an economic slowdown, shifting focus to high-priority areas like cloud infrastructure.

title: |​​The Top 10 Fastest-Growing Cities in Washington State
summary: Washington State is experiencing significant population growth, with Redfin identifying the top 10 fastest-growing cities based on a 5-year population increase from 2017 to 2021. Redmond leads the list with an 18% growth, followed by Lacey and Richland. The article provides median sale prices, average rent, and local attractions for each city to help those considering a move to the Evergreen State.

title: 7 Apps for a more productive ‘work from home’ experience
summary: This article reviews seven applications designed to enhance productivity for remote workers, moving beyond common tools like Zoom and Slack. It highlights apps such as Basecamp for project management, Freedom for distraction blocking, Krisp for noise cancellation, Evernote for digital note-taking, Simplish for to-do lists, Dashlane for password management, and Zapier for automating repetitive tasks. The author, Adarsh, provides a brief overview of each app's features and benefits for improving the work-from-home experience.

title: Sonoff ZBDongle-E Zigbee 3.0 USB dongle features EFR32MG21 MCU with +20dBm radio
summary: ITEAD has launched the Sonoff ZBDongle-E, a new Zigbee 3.0 USB adapter featuring a Silicon Labs EFR32MG21 Arm Cortex-M33 microcontroller with a powerful +20dBm radio for extended range. This dongle serves as an alternative to the popular ZBDongle-P and is pre-flashed with Zigbee coordinator firmware, making it compatible with various home automation platforms like Home Assistant, Zigbee2MQTT, and OpenHAB. It can also be re-flashed for use as a Zigbee Router or with OpenThread/Spinel RCP firmware to support Thread and Matter standards.

title: Atlassian appoints Microsoft’s Joe Binz as CFO
summary: Atlassian has appointed Joe Binz, formerly of Microsoft, as its new Chief Financial Officer, effective September 6, 2022. Co-CEO Scott Farquhar expressed excitement for Binz's expertise in capital allocation, emphasizing that while Binz brings new experience, the company's core philosophy and interaction with shareholders will remain consistent. This announcement coincides with Atlassian's FY2022 Q4 results, which showed a 36% year-on-year total revenue growth to $759.8 million, despite a slight slowdown in converting free customers to paying ones.

title: Large Indiana employers Eli Lilly and Cummins speak out about the state's new restrictive abortion law
summary: Large Indiana employers Eli Lilly and Cummins have voiced strong opposition to the state's newly passed restrictive abortion law. Eli Lilly stated the law would hinder its ability to attract diverse talent and force it to plan for employment growth outside Indiana, while Cummins expressed concerns about its impact on talent attraction and retention. Both companies emphasized that the law conflicts with ensuring women's full participation in the workforce and the need for inclusive environments.

title: Suffered Attack, Paid Ransom, Restored Systems: The CNA’s Ransomware Timeline
summary: CNA Financial Corp., a major U.S. insurance company, reportedly paid $40 million in ransom to cybercriminals after being hit by a ransomware attack on March 21, 2021. The attack disrupted some of its systems, but the company claims to have fully restored operations by May 2021. Industry experts express mixed opinions, with some questioning CNA's failure to detect the attack and the substantial ransom paid.

title: Poly Rove DECT Wireless Phones now Microsoft Teams supported with Teams SIP Gateway
summary: Poly has announced that its Rove DECT Wireless IP Phone Solution is now certified for Microsoft Teams via the Teams SIP Gateway. This integration allows industries like retail and manufacturing, heavy users of DECT, to register their devices directly to the Microsoft Teams cloud SIP gateway, potentially eliminating the need for on-premises PBXs or certified Session Border Controllers. Poly's Rove 30 and Rove 40 handsets, along with B2 and B4 bases, are ruggedized, IP65-rated, and feature Microban antimicrobial protection, offering specialized solutions for various work environments.

title: Putting the emphasis on IEC 62368-1 Overvoltage Compliance
summary: The article discusses the importance of complying with the IEC 62368-1 standard for electronic equipment, especially concerning overvoltage and overcurrent protection in universal power adapters. It highlights how this newer, hazard-based standard is more flexible and future-proof than its predecessors, requiring careful consideration of protection components like varistors, GDTs, and fuses. The authors, from Littelfuse, Inc., detail the scope, criteria, and testing functions required by IEC 62368-1, offering guidance on selecting appropriate protection components for reliable and safe electronic designs.

title: Is the Vanguard MSCI International ETF (VGS) a good alternative to global tech shares?
summary: This article examines the Vanguard MSCI International ETF (VGS) as a potential alternative to direct investment in global tech shares. It highlights that VGS includes a significant allocation to information technology (21.5%) and offers broad diversification across 1,473 businesses globally with a low management fee of 0.18%. While VGS provides diversified tech exposure, the article also mentions other ETFs like iShares S&P 500 ETF and Betashares Nasdaq 100 ETF for greater or more targeted tech sector concentration.

title: AI as Watchdog: how it can harm, how to control it
summary: This article examines the dual nature of AI in surveillance, highlighting its potential for both harm and good. It discusses how AI is already extensively used by governments for tracking individuals, citing examples from China and Israel, and argues that while AI surveillance cannot be stopped, its use can be regulated. The author suggests that democracy, in its truest form, is the "anti-venom" against the misuse of AI surveillance.

title: Cybersecurity skills shortage provides rare cross-training opportunities
summary: The article highlights the significant cybersecurity skills shortage in the U.S., presenting it as a unique opportunity for individuals to cross-train and enter a high-paying field. It discusses the attributes that make a good cybersecurity analyst, dispels the myth that a college degree is always required, and outlines various certification paths, including those for cloud security and zero trust frameworks, emphasizing the benefits for both individuals and global security.

title: An oil company is seeking property tax breaks to finance its plans to remove carbon dioxide from Texas skies
summary: Occidental Petroleum is seeking significant property tax breaks in Texas to finance its ambitious plans for large-scale direct air capture projects aimed at removing carbon dioxide from the atmosphere. These projects, potentially worth tens of billions of dollars, would be the first commercial-scale operations of a technology that is currently expensive and has raised concerns among some environmentalists about its effectiveness and potential impacts. The company plans to use the captured carbon dioxide for enhanced oil recovery and to sell carbon offsets, leveraging federal and state incentives to make the projects viable.

title: Nvidia warns of lower second-quarter revenue on gaming weakness
summary: Nvidia Corp warned of a 19% drop in second-quarter revenue from the prior quarter due to weakness in its gaming business, sending its shares down by about 8%. This follows similar warnings from other chipmakers and is attributed to consumers weighing purchases of discretionary items amidst economic concerns, as well as continued supply chain issues. The company expects to report overall Q2 revenue of approximately $6.70 billion, significantly below analyst estimates.

title: 10 malicious Python packages exposed in latest repository attack
summary: Check Point Research has discovered 10 new malicious packages in PyPi, the official Python repository, which could lead to malware downloads or credential theft for unsuspecting users. These supply-chain attacks are becoming increasingly common, prompting repositories like GitHub to implement digital signing systems for packages to help verify their authenticity. One such package, "ascii2text," mimicked a legitimate library and downloaded a malicious script to steal tokens, passwords, and crypto wallet information.

title: NVIDIA Announces Major Release of Omniverse With New USD Connectors and Tools, Simulation Technologies and Developer Frameworks
summary: NVIDIA has announced a major update to its Omniverse platform, introducing new developer frameworks, tools, apps, and plugins designed to build and connect metaverse worlds. These enhancements include AI-powered tools like Omniverse Avatar Cloud Engine, DeepSearch, and NeuralVDB, along with 11 new USD Connectors to integrate with leading 3D applications and CAD software. The updates aim to simplify virtual world creation and foster collaboration across industries, bridging the physical and virtual realms.

title: Red Dead Redemption 2 & GTA V could be debuting on Xbox Cloud Gaming very soon, per Rockstar Support
summary: Rockstar Support's website suggests that Red Dead Redemption 2 and GTA V may soon be available on Xbox Cloud Gaming for users who own the digital versions and have an Xbox Game Pass Ultimate subscription. Microsoft had briefly listed the games in its Cloud Gaming catalog, leading to speculation of their imminent arrival. However, Microsoft later stated this was a bug and the listings have since been removed.

title: Salesforce Inc. stock falls Tuesday, underperforms market
