summary: Salesforce Inc. (CRM) shares fell 3.96% on Tuesday, closing at $182.24, underperforming the broader market as the S&P 500 and Dow Jones also declined. This marked the third consecutive day of losses for the stock, placing it significantly below its 52-week high. Salesforce also lagged behind some competitors, with Microsoft Corp. rising while Adobe Inc. and SAP SE ADR experienced smaller declines.

title: Security for next generation telecommunication networks
summary: Microsoft emphasizes security as a first principle in developing networks and systems for next-generation telecommunication, particularly 5G and 6G, by adopting a zero-trust security architecture. The article details how the disaggregated software components in modern telecom networks increase the attack surface and how Microsoft Azure's massive scale and sophisticated defenses, including AI/ML and cloud security capabilities, are leveraged to protect against threats to Open RAN architecture and critical infrastructure. It also addresses strategies for mitigating the impact of compromised systems through rapid detection and recovery mechanisms.

title: SoFi launches first-of-its-kind web3 ETF
summary: SoFi has launched its first-of-its-kind Web 3 ETF (TWEB), providing investors access to companies powering the next tech revolution, including the metaverse and artificial intelligence. The ETF tracks the SoFi Solactive ARTIS® Web 3.0 Index, diversifying investments across 40 securities in NFTs & Tokenization, Blockchain Technology, Metaverse, and Big Data & AI. The article also highlights various risks associated with investing in these rapidly evolving technologies.

title: Beelink SER5 Review – An AMD Ryzen 5 5600H mini PC tested with Windows 11, Ubuntu 22.04
summary: This article reviews the Beelink SER5 mini PC, equipped with an AMD Ryzen 5 5600H processor, 32GB DDR4 RAM, and a 500GB NVMe SSD. The author details the hardware, installation processes, and performance benchmarks for both Windows 11 and Ubuntu 22.04. The review concludes that while the SER5 offers very good performance, it should be considered an alternative to the SER4 rather than a significant upgrade due to similar performance metrics, with Ubuntu often outperforming Windows in gaming.

title: Ant Group IPO: Everything you need to know about Ant Group
summary: Ant Group's IPO plans are currently on hold as the company focuses on business rectification and optimization, with previous attempts to go public having been shelved. Despite a significant drop in its valuation from $315 billion to $180 billion, Ant Group remains profitable and generates revenue primarily through its lending, investment, and insurance products, with Alipay serving as a crucial entry point for users into its extensive ecosystem. The company faces stiff competition from Tencent's WeChat Pay in the Chinese digital payment market and is undergoing regulatory changes, including an anticipated shift in control from Jack Ma and increased oversight from the People's Bank of China.

title: Spotify starts selling live music tickets to fans directly
summary: Spotify has launched a new website to sell live concert tickets directly to fans, moving away from exclusively redirecting users to third-party partners like Ticketmaster. This new platform, currently in a testing phase, lists upcoming gigs primarily in the U.S. and allows users to purchase tickets with a Spotify account, aiming to improve event discovery and potentially generate revenue beyond streaming. The company has not yet disclosed details on booking fees or how this new initiative integrates with its existing live events features.

title: Megazone Cloud receives $343 mn from MBK, IMM PE in Series C funding
summary: Megazone Cloud, South Korea’s largest managed cloud service provider, has closed its Series C funding round with 450 billion won ($343 million) from MBK Partners and IMM Private Equity. This investment, combined with an earlier one from KT Corp., brings the company's valuation to 2.4 trillion won, making it a unicorn. Megazone Cloud is also preparing for an IPO by the end of 2023.

title: Microsoft Sues “Black Market” Software Distributor for TM and Copyright Infringement
summary: Microsoft Corporation has filed a lawsuit against The Search People Enterprises Ltd. and its principal for copyright and trademark infringement. The suit alleges the defendants are distributing "black market" access devices for Microsoft software, which they falsely advertise as genuine. Microsoft conducted over two dozen test purchases to confirm the illegality and is seeking a permanent injunction and damages.

title: Russian hacking group claims attack on Lockheed Martin
summary: A prominent Russian hacking group called Killnet claims responsibility for a DDoS attack that took Lockheed Martin's websites offline. The group stated its motivation was Lockheed Martin's provision of M142 High Mobility Artillery Rocket Systems to Ukraine and also claims to have stolen information on Lockheed Martin employees. Lockheed Martin denies any system compromise, while Killnet's founder issued a chilling warning of escalating attacks.

title: Johnson Controls AI-enhanced OpenBlue Platform Cuts Microsoft's Beijing Campus Energy Footprint
summary: Johnson Controls partnered with Microsoft to implement its AI-enhanced OpenBlue platform at the Microsoft Beijing Campus, resulting in significant energy savings of 27.9%. This collaboration involved upgrading chiller systems and integrating various building systems onto the Azure platform as a central "digital brain," which, combined with Johnson Controls' OpenBlue Enterprise Manager, has led to improved operational efficiency and a substantial reduction in energy consumption. This success has earned the campus energy saving endorsements and financial subsidies from local governments.

title: How Microsoft secures its spot among the world's most valuable brands
summary: Microsoft has become one of the world's most valuable brands, with its brand value reaching $661 billion in 2022, securing the number four spot in Kantar BrandZ Most Valuable Global Brands. The company's success is attributed to its meaningful, different, and salient offerings, including superior cloud, software, and hardware products, as well as its commitment to sustainability. Under CEO Satya Nadella, Microsoft has focused on specific market segments, leading to a tenfold increase in brand value and solidifying its position as the world's most valuable business services brand, further boosted by the continued digital transformation and remote work trends.

title: Launch builds on 2020 program which marked first-in-the-US agreement with corporate partners to reduce business travel emissions through sustainable aviation fuels.
summary: Alaska Airlines has launched a new program to accelerate the adoption of sustainable aviation fuels (SAF) by engaging corporate partners, including Microsoft, Boeing, and Washington State University. This initiative aims to expand education and awareness about SAF, provide SAF credits to corporate customers, and foster collaboration to overcome barriers to scaling SAF production. The program builds on a 2020 agreement with Microsoft and is part of Alaska's broader commitment to achieve net-zero carbon emissions by 2040.

title: Why 2023 is the year of passwordless authentication
summary: The article argues that 2023 should be the year of passwordless authentication due to increasing password vulnerabilities and user friction with traditional methods. It highlights the benefits of FIDO-based passwordless authentication, which uses public-key cryptography and biometrics/PINs, making it more secure and convenient than passwords or MFA. Despite being standardized since 2019, IAM vendors and startups are now widely implementing these solutions, with surveys showing significant positive impacts on risk reduction, user experience, and IT efficiency.

title: Johnson Controls AI-enhanced OpenBlue Platform Cuts Microsoft's Beijing Campus Energy Footprint
summary: Johnson Controls partnered with Microsoft Beijing Campus to implement its AI-enhanced OpenBlue platform, resulting in significant energy savings of 27.9% and 98% uptime for key equipment. This collaboration helped the campus receive an energy-saving endorsement and subsidy from the Beijing Municipal Government, highlighting the potential of advanced technology for sustainable building operations and carbon emission reduction. The project demonstrates a successful application of AI and integrated building management systems in achieving net-zero goals.

title: Thematic Investing: 3 Key Trends in Cybersecurity
summary: This article examines three key trends shaping the cybersecurity industry: increasing costs of data breaches, new vulnerabilities created by remote work, and the role of AI in reducing breach costs. It highlights the financial impact of cybercrime and data breaches on businesses and illustrates how AI-based solutions are becoming crucial for detection and response. The article also introduces the Global X Cybersecurity ETF (BUG) for investors interested in this sector.

title: Johnson Controls partners Microsoft Beijing Campus for optimization of building operations
summary: Johnson Controls has partnered with Microsoft Beijing Campus for the retrofit and optimization of its building operations, resulting in 27.9% energy savings and 98% key equipment uptime. This initiative, which involved implementing AI-enhanced OpenBlue Net Zero Buildings solutions and upgrading chiller systems, has earned the campus an energy saving endorsement and financial subsidy from the Beijing Municipal Government. It showcases how advanced technology can significantly reduce energy consumption and emissions in existing buildings, contributing to China's carbon neutrality goals.

title: Crawler Hints supports Microsoft’s IndexNow in helping users find new content
summary: Cloudflare's Crawler Hints now supports Microsoft's IndexNow protocol, allowing websites to proactively notify search engines of content changes. This "push" model for indexing aims to significantly reduce wasted crawler traffic, saving bandwidth and compute resources for both websites and search engines, and improving content freshness in search results. Cloudflare plans to default Crawler Hints on for all customers and hopes for wider adoption of the IndexNow standard by other major search engines like Google.

title: The Forrester Wave™: Anti-Money Laundering Solutions, Q2 2025
summary: SAS has been recognized as a leader in The Forrester Wave™: Anti-Money Laundering Solutions, Q2 2025 report. Forrester notes that SAS's recent acquisition of Hazy synthetic data software is expected to enhance its Financial Crime Compliance portfolio, especially with large data models and Generative AI. The report highlights SAS's AML solution as suitable for enterprises with existing SAS and data science skills, emphasizing its strong framework for quantifying ROI.

title: Why Microsoft Courts Nigerian Digital ID4D
summary: Microsoft Corporation has expressed its willingness to partner with Nigeria's Digital Identification for Development (ID4D) project, focusing on capacity development and data protection. This collaboration aims to support the ID4D project's efforts in strengthening digital identity and data security within Nigeria. The ID4D project coordinator, Musa Odole Solomon, welcomed Microsoft's interest, particularly in capacity building for ecosystem partners and in establishing robust data protection laws.

title: Microsoft, Traeger Grills and Young Living are cutting staff. Are Utah workers in for more layoffs?
summary: Several companies with a presence in Utah, including Traeger Grills, Young Living Essential Oils, and Microsoft, are implementing staff layoffs due to reduced consumer spending from inflation and ongoing supply chain issues. Traeger is cutting 14% of its global workforce, and Young Living is reducing staff by about 200 people. Despite these reductions, a labor economist from the University of Utah emphasizes that layoffs are still relatively rare in the current strong economy, with overall layoff rates remaining low compared to historic averages.

title: Up Close at Defcon 30 in Las Vegas
summary: PCMag staffers attended Defcon 30 in Las Vegas, a significant annual gathering for hackers, to gain insights into current cybersecurity trends and hands-on experience. The event, in its 30th year, facilitated networking among security professionals and provided a platform to discuss pressing issues like insider threats and Windows vulnerabilities. Staffers highlighted the conference's community-focused atmosphere and practical demonstrations.

title: Acquisitive backup crew N-able buys Spinpanel
summary: N-able, a backup service supplier for MSPs and CSPs, has acquired Spinpanel, a company specializing in Microsoft 365 management and automation for CSPs. This acquisition aims to enhance N-able's cloud product offerings for partners and provide Spinpanel customers with broader IT management and security solutions. Concurrently, N-able announced its second-quarter revenues of $91.6 million, a 7 percent year-on-year increase, and a significant profit of $4.3 million.

title: Buffett's Berkshire boosts Ally, Activision holdings; sheds Verizon
summary: Berkshire Hathaway significantly increased its stakes in Ally Financial and Activision Blizzard while completely exiting its investment in Verizon Communications by June 30. The conglomerate, run by Warren Buffett, also slowed its overall stock buying in the second quarter, making fewer new purchases and sales compared to the first quarter. Berkshire's portfolio continues to be dominated by Apple, with substantial investments in oil companies Chevron and Occidental Petroleum.

title: Saudi PIF buys shares in Alphabet, Zoom and Microsoft in U.S. shopping spree
summary: Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund (PIF) has significantly increased its U.S. stock holdings, acquiring shares in major tech companies like Alphabet, Zoom Video, and Microsoft. The sovereign wealth fund also invested in JPMorgan, BlackRock, Starbucks, and several other prominent companies. These investments are part of the PIF's strategy to diversify Saudi Arabia's economy away from oil and build an international investment portfolio.

title: John Deere tractors are getting the jailbreak treatment from hackers
summary: Hackers are now jailbreaking John Deere tractors, highlighting the broader "right-to-repair" issue beyond smartphones. A hacker, "Sick Codes," demonstrated at Def Con how to access and control John Deere tractors' onboard systems, revealing vulnerabilities and the importance for farmers to be able to repair their own software. This development underscores the need to balance farmers' access to essential machinery systems with industry-wide security to prevent agricultural disruptions.

title: Here’s Why We’re Moving All Simulation Solves to the Cloud
summary: Autodesk Fusion 360 is transitioning all simulation solves for Linear Static stress, Modal, Thermal, and Thermal stress study types to the cloud starting September 2022. This shift aims to enhance user productivity by allowing multiple simulations to run concurrently without tying up local machines, and to improve performance by leveraging cloud infrastructure. The move aligns with the Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) approach to provide faster results and better scalability, while Linear Static simulation remains included at no extra cost for subscribers.

title: EY Canada adds Microsoft Dynamics team from DXC Technology
summary: EY Canada has acquired a team of Microsoft Dynamics professionals from DXC Technology, with over a dozen experts joining EY offices in Toronto, Calgary, and Vancouver. This move aims to expand EY Canada's Microsoft Dynamics practice, enhancing its services in modernizing finance, operations, ERP, and supply chain management for clients. This strategic acquisition follows other recent technology firm purchases by EY Canada, bolstering its digital capabilities to assist businesses in implementing custom solutions and software applications.

title: Four Budget-friendly Tech Upgrades Every Hospital Executive Should Know About
summary: Hospitals have faced significant strain, exacerbated by the COVID-19 pandemic, leading to budget and compatibility issues with hastily adopted technologies. This article highlights four budget-friendly tech upgrades—cloud computing, remote patient monitoring, automated scheduling, and foundational infrastructure improvements—that can enhance efficiency, attract a modern workforce, and improve patient outcomes without requiring a complete system overhaul. The emphasis is on incremental digital transformation to better manage data, streamline operations, and prepare for future demands in healthcare.

title: Saudi PIF buys shares in Alphabet, Zoom and Microsoft in US shopping spree
summary: Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund (PIF) significantly expanded its US stock portfolio in the second quarter, investing approximately $40.8 billion. The fund acquired shares in major tech companies like Alphabet, Zoom Video, and Microsoft, alongside holdings in JPMorgan, BlackRock, Starbucks, Adobe, and others. The PIF, managing $620 billion in assets, is a key instrument in Saudi Arabia's strategy to diversify its economy away from oil.

title: Microsoft launches Dev Box preview for developers to try cloud-based workstations
summary: Microsoft has launched a public preview of its Dev Box service, offering developers cloud-based, ready-to-code workstations. Built on Windows 365, this managed service provides virtual machines with eight virtual CPUs and 32GB of RAM, supporting various IDEs and SDKs for cross-platform app development. Organizations can try 15 hours of free usage monthly, with consumption-based billing thereafter.

title: PTC Channel Chief Stuart Heavyside On The ‘Massive’ SaaS Opportunity And Why Digital Marketing Is Key To Partner Success
summary: PTC Channel Chief Stuart Heavyside emphasizes the significant revenue growth opportunity for partners in the transition to Software as a Service (SaaS). He details PTC's strategic shift to SaaS for core products like Windchill and Creo, highlighting the importance of customer success and digital marketing for partner profitability. Heavyside asserts that the SaaS market for PLM is projected to double, presenting a massive opportunity for partners to earn substantially more per license dollar with increased service revenue.

title: Should we break up Facebook to save it?
summary: Richard J. Shinder argues that Facebook's recent financial struggles and user dissatisfaction stemming from a degraded user experience, content moderation issues, and privacy scandals highlight the need for a drastic change. He proposes breaking up Meta Platforms into two entities: a "good bank" Facebook focusing on its original social media strengths and apolitical content moderation, and a "bad bank" Meta for its more experimental and data-driven ventures like the metaverse. This bifurcation, he suggests, would allow users to choose their preferred experience, maximize shareholder value, and potentially salvage the "good" aspects of the platform.

title: Capital Budgets Fall to 13% of IT Spending
summary: Capital budgets now constitute only 13% of IT spending in North American companies, a significant drop from 24% in 2013, as businesses shift away from on-premises infrastructure towards public cloud and subscription-based applications. While total IT spending is projected to increase, the allocation is largely towards operational expenditures like cloud infrastructure and applications rather than long-term capital investments. This shift brings flexibility but also risks of being locked into difficult-to-negotiate operational contracts.

title: Startup Digs Into Public Filings With GPU-Driven Machine Learning to Serve Up Alternative Financial Data Services
summary: Intrinio, a startup based in St. Petersburg, Fla., uses GPU-driven machine learning to parse publicly available financial data, offering an alternative to traditional, bundled financial data products. Co-founded by Rachel Carpenter and Joseph French, Intrinio provides à la carte subscription services for equities, options, estimates, ETFs, and ESG data, making it more affordable and accessible for fintech innovators and startups. The company's technology significantly reduces errors and streamlines data cleansing and standardization, allowing clients like Robinhood, FTX, and Aiera to integrate high-quality financial data into their platforms.

title: Microsoft plans to shut down its Olympia Corp test lab for Windows Enterprise
summary: Microsoft Corporation is closing its 'Olympia Corp' program, a test lab designed for Windows enterprise users to test business-oriented features. Participants were notified via email about the impending shutdown, effective September 12, 2022, and advised to back up any data. Launched in 2017, the program helped Microsoft gather feedback for enterprise Windows versions, but the company now believes other simulations and demos can achieve similar goals.

title: Amazon (AWS) and Microsoft Data Centers in Virginia
summary: This article details the extensive presence of Amazon Web Services (AWS) and Microsoft data centers across Virginia, highlighting locations in both Northern Virginia and emerging areas like Boydton. It outlines specific data center sites, their sizes, and ongoing development plans for both companies, emphasizing their investments and strategic growth in the region. The report also covers their respective cloud regions, availability zones, and cloud on-ramps to support demand for compute, storage, and database capabilities.

title: Bill Gates Is Ecolab’s Largest Shareholder. He Just Scooped Up More Shares.
summary: Bill Gates, through his investment vehicles, has increased his stake in Ecolab, a company specializing in water-treatment, hygiene, and infection-prevention services. He is already the largest shareholder of Ecolab, which provides essential services related to public health and safety. This recent acquisition further solidifies his position as a major investor in the company.

title: Digital Health Market Is Booming Worldwide | GE Healthcare, Philips Healthcare, Qualcomm, Cerner Corp
summary: The Global Digital Health Market is experiencing significant growth, as detailed in a new research study by HTF Market Intelligence Consulting Pvt. Ltd. The report evaluates market risks, identifies opportunities, and offers strategic decision-making support, covering market trends, growth drivers, technologies, and investment structures. Key players in this booming market include GE Healthcare, Philips Healthcare, Qualcomm, and Cerner Corp, among others, with the market segmented by areas like mHealth, Tele Healthcare, Healthcare Analytics, and Digital Health Systems across more than 18 countries.

title: Aflac virtualizes the customer enrollment experience
summary: Aflac successfully virtualized its customer enrollment experience during the pandemic to support its independent agents, who were facing significant business risks due to social distancing. By combining existing technologies and building a new enrollment platform on AWS, Aflac enabled agents to conduct virtual meetings, co-browse with clients, and process policy purchases more efficiently. This digital transformation, which included the development of microsites and a "bionic" agent approach, earned Aflac a CIO 100 Award and lays the groundwork for a full migration to the cloud and further intelligent automation.

title: No, Microsoft did not acquire Sony
summary: A widespread but fake news report claimed that Microsoft had acquired Sony for $130 billion, including all its divisions like Sony Music and PlayStation. The article debunks this claim, citing the lack of credible media coverage, absence of official statements from either company, and the complex regulatory approvals such a deal would require.

title: Why the ESG/Tech Combination Is Important
summary: Broad market environmental, social, and governance (ESG) exchange-traded funds (ETFs) frequently have significant allocations to technology stocks. For example, the Invesco ESG Nasdaq 100 ETF (QQMG) has a technology weight of almost 62%. While some critics view this as over-reliance on tech, experts argue that technology companies often embody sustainable development principles, making them suitable for ESG funds despite facing scrutiny on issues like data privacy and energy consumption.

title: Online gaming – No mere child’s play
summary: This article explores the growth and impact of online gaming, which has seen an explosion in popularity, particularly in India. It delves into both the benefits, such as improved attention and social connection for some, and the significant risks, including health problems like 'gamer's thumb,' obesity, vision issues, seizures, and the psychological impact of gaming disorder, even touching on dangerous games like the "Blue Whale suicide game." The author emphasizes the importance of integrating gaming into a healthy lifestyle to avoid addiction and negative consequences.

title: Saudi Arabia is first country to approve Microsoft purchase of Activision Blizzard
summary: Saudi Arabia has become the first country to approve Microsoft's acquisition of Activision Blizzard, despite ongoing investigations in other nations concerning potential competition issues. The Saudi government issued a "No Objection" certificate, facilitating the merger. This approval is significant as Saudi Arabia is a major shareholder in Activision Blizzard and has been increasing its investment in the gaming industry.

title: Microsoft named a Leader in 2022 Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for Data Integration Tools
summary: Microsoft has been recognized as a Leader in the 2022 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Data Integration Tools, signifying its ongoing commitment to comprehensive and cost-effective data integration solutions. The company's offerings, including Azure Data Factory and Azure Synapse Link, provide end-to-end data integration strategies to help organizations manage and gain insights from their rapidly growing data. This recognition highlights Microsoft's focus on empowering businesses to achieve competitive advantages and better outcomes through data.

title: 15 Best Apps That Can Pay You Real Money
summary: This article lists 15 best apps that can help users earn real money, ranging from market research apps like Money App and iPoll to freelance platforms like Upwork and Fiverr, and social media platforms like YouTube, Facebook, and Instagram for content monetization. It explains various methods to leverage these apps for income, such as affiliate marketing, selling products, participating in surveys, and investment savings, while also highlighting general ways to earn extra income and the benefits of having multiple income streams.

title: Warner Music’s HipHopDX Asia Launches ‘The Regionals’ – The First-Ever Pan-Asia Cypher Series
summary: Warner Music's HipHopDX Asia has launched 'The Regionals,' a pioneering pan-Asia rap cypher series designed to globalize Asian hip-hop music. This initiative brings together top emcees from various Eastern markets and pairs them with acclaimed Western hip-hop producers like !llmind, Hit-Boy, and 9th Wonder. The project aims to showcase diverse talent, connect global hip-hop communities, and promote Asian hip-hop culture worldwide, with the first cyphers scheduled for release in September.

title: These Wide-Moat Stocks Are Gaining Ground
summary: Quality stocks with wide economic moats, including Microsoft and Amazon, have outperformed since the bear market low in June, despite still being undervalued. While narrow-moat stocks have seen stronger recent gains due to market-cap weighting of companies like Apple and Tesla, wide-moat companies are better positioned to handle inflation due to their pricing power. Overall, Morningstar analysts consider wide-moat stocks to be deeply undervalued compared to overpriced narrow-moat stocks.

title: What’s Changed: 2022 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Data Integration Tools
summary: Gartner's 2022 Magic Quadrant for Data Integration Tools highlights renewed momentum in the data integration market, driven by hybrid/multicloud needs, augmented data management, and data fabric designs. The report notes a shift from mega-vendors to niche players, with Informatica retaining its leadership position, and new entrants like AWS, Palantir, and Software AG joining the quadrant. Key market drivers include augmented data integration, increased data engineering requirements, and DataOps.

title: Pleb Miner Month Celebrates The Rise Of Home Bitcoin Miners
summary: Pleb Miner Month, organized by Jon and Sarah DiGiacomo and MaxBitBuyBit, will highlight small-scale and home Bitcoin miners throughout September. The initiative aims to decentralize Bitcoin mining discussions, moving away from large corporate events, and will feature interviews, educational content, and raffles of mining equipment. The month-long celebration emphasizes that Bitcoin mining began at home with Satoshi Nakamoto and that individual "pleb miners" are crucial for securing the network's decentralization and upholding its foundational principles.

title: Rackspace’s intention not to sell leaves Wall Street wary
summary: Rackspace Technology Inc. has decided against selling the company and will instead pursue a restructuring plan, disappointing some Wall Street analysts. The cloud-computing services provider, the largest tech company in San Antonio, will realign into separate business units for private and public clouds. This decision led to a significant drop in share prices as analysts downgraded the stock, expressing skepticism about the standalone strategy's ability to create shareholder value quickly.

title: PR News | Ex-Bush II Aide Lands at Truist Financial - Thu., Aug. 25, 2022
summary: Scott Stanzel, a former communications official in the George W. Bush White House, has been appointed as EVP and CCO of Truist Financial Corporation, effective October 1. He will lead corporate communications from the Charlotte, NC headquarters, overseeing internal and external communications. Stanzel brings a wealth of experience from previous roles at Capital One, Amazon, and Microsoft.

title: Compass CTO is out; brokerage laying off tech employees
summary: Compass has parted ways with its Chief Technology Officer, Joseph Sirosh, and is laying off a "small" number of tech employees and recruiters as part of a $320 million cost-cutting initiative. This move signifies a shift for Compass, emphasizing its role as a residential brokerage rather than solely a technology company, despite having invested heavily in its tech platform. Kendra Shimmell and Shay Artzi will take over some of Sirosh's duties, though his CTO position will not be directly replaced.

title: Newegg Joins Intel Gamer Days with Deals on CPUs, Gaming PCs and Laptops
summary: Newegg is participating in Intel Gamer Days, offering promotional sales on Intel processors, gaming PCs, and laptops from August 25 to September 4. The event includes livestreams, exclusive deals, and a sweepstakes to win a custom PC valued over $3,400, powered by a 12th Gen Intel Core i9-12900K processor. Customers purchasing eligible products will also receive complimentary game codes for Arcadegeddon or Call of Duty: Modern Warfare II.

title: Microsoft Wants Uber Drivers’ Facial Recognition Privacy Case Tossed on Jurisdictional Grounds
summary: Microsoft has filed a motion seeking to dismiss remaining biometric privacy claims against it regarding Uber's use of its facial recognition technology, "Real Time ID Check." The company argues that Illinois courts lack general or specific jurisdiction over it as Microsoft is headquartered in Washington and incorporated in Delaware, and its technology does not specifically target Illinois. The plaintiffs, Illinois-based Uber drivers, allege that the consentless capture of their faceprints by Uber through Microsoft's technology violates the Illinois Biometric Information Privacy Act (BIPA).

title: Cisco Delivers Enterprise Architecture for Voice, Video and Integrated Data Networks
summary: Cisco Systems announced Cisco AVVID (Architecture for Voice, Video and Integrated Data) for corporate enterprises, aiming to enable Internet-based business models with a lower total cost of ownership. This architecture is a culmination of Cisco's multiservice strategy, featuring IP infrastructure, call processing, New World applications, and intelligent IP-enabled clients. Cisco AVVID is designed to provide a flexible, converged network solution, highlighting network availability, open systems, and the rapid deployment of advanced applications.

title: Eyeing expansion, Infosys leases 5 lakh square feet in Bengaluru
summary: Infosys has leased approximately 5 lakh square feet of office space in Bengaluru to support its expansion plans, which will help the company spread its presence across the city. This move is part of Infosys's strategy to expand beyond its existing campuses and set up new offices in tier-2 cities like Kolkata, Nagpur, Coimbatore, Vizag, and Noida, aiming to tap into a wider talent pool and accommodate its growing employee count, which reached 335,186 by June 2022. The new facility, located at Northgate, will provide space for around 1,000 employees as part of the company's hybrid work model.

title: Amazon not expected to bid for Electronic Arts, says CNBC
summary: CNBC reported that Amazon.com Inc is not expected to bid for Electronic Arts Inc, refuting an earlier report about a potential takeover. This news caused EA's stock to fluctuate, initially jumping 15% on the acquisition rumor before settling to a 4% gain. Amazon has recently been active in acquisitions, diversifying its business, while analysts see EA as an attractive target due to its strong licenses and metaverse potential, despite a struggling global gaming industry.

title: Making European Cloud Providers More Competitive
summary: Microsoft is introducing changes to its software licensing terms, effective October 1, 2022, to enhance the competitiveness of European cloud providers. These updates aim to make it easier for customers to port their software, ensure partners have access to cost-effective solutions, and empower partners to build hosted solutions efficiently. The initiative reflects Microsoft's commitment to a fair and open competitive cloud economy in Europe.

title: Microsoft Korea introduces its new startup program ‘Microsoft Launcher’
summary: Microsoft Korea launched "Microsoft Launcher," a new program designed to support local startups at every stage of their growth. This platform offers benefits valued up to ₩500,000,000, including technology, tools, Azure credits, and mentorship, aiming to address common challenges faced by Korean startups. The initiative is part of Microsoft's broader effort to foster a healthy digital ecosystem in Asia, a region recognized as a global innovation powerhouse.

title: How Royal Caribbean set up a seafaring cloud strategy
summary: Royal Caribbean Group has adopted a multicloud strategy to manage the complex IT needs of its cruise ship fleet, leveraging Google Cloud, AWS, and Microsoft Azure for different workloads. This approach helps address the unique challenges of seafaring operations, such as unreliable satellite connectivity and the need for robust hybrid solutions. The company emphasizes the importance of balancing internal expertise with external partners and carefully considering cost and talent access in its vendor selection process.

title: How to Get Windows 11 on HP Computers
summary: This article provides a comprehensive guide on how to upgrade HP computers to Windows 11. It covers the benefits of upgrading, the essential system requirements, and step-by-step instructions for installation via Windows Update or the Windows 11 Installation Assistant. Additionally, it offers advice on preparing the computer for installation, backing up files, and troubleshooting common issues after the upgrade.

title: Data breach at Nelnet exposes 2.5 million student loan records
summary: Nelnet Serving, a division of Nelnet, experienced a data breach affecting 2.5 million student loan records from the Oklahoma Student Loan Authority and EdFinancial Services LLC. The breach, which occurred between June and July 2022, potentially exposed names, addresses, email addresses, phone numbers, and Social Security numbers. Law enforcement and the U.S. Department of Education were notified, and several class-action lawsuits are reportedly being prepared despite the company offering identity theft protection services to affected individuals.

title: Tencent, Sony Collectively Acquire 30 Percent Of Elden Ring Developer From Software
summary: Tencent and Sony Interactive Entertainment have collectively acquired approximately 30% of From Software, the developer behind games like Elden Ring and the Dark Souls series. Tencent's subsidiary, Sixjoy Hong Kong, bought 16.25% of shares, and SIE acquired 14.09%, though Kadokawa Corporation remains the majority shareholder with 69.66%. This investment aims to bolster From Software's development capabilities and expand its global publishing reach for its game IPs.

title: Netflix hires two top ad executives from Snap
summary: Netflix has hired Jeremi Gorman as president of worldwide advertising and Peter Naylor as vice president of ad sales, both formerly top executives at Snap Inc. These strategic hires signal Netflix's serious commitment to launching an ad-supported streaming service next year, leveraging Gorman and Naylor's strong relationships with brands and advertisers from their previous roles at Snap and Amazon.

title: VMware CEO weighs in on Broadcom acquisition, multicloud and why supercloud is the future
summary: VMware CEO Raghu Raghuram discussed the planned Broadcom acquisition, his company's multicloud strategy, and the evolution toward supercloud, emphasizing that Broadcom sees VMware as a valuable asset rather than just a numbers-driven deal. He highlighted VMware's early bet on multicloud starting in 2018 and the introduction of VMware Aria, a true multicloud management solution that federates data sources in real-time using GraphQL. Raghuram stressed that Aria differentiates itself by pulling data directly across various clouds, rather than acting as an interface for separate products.

title: NetEase is acquiring Heavy Rain developer Quantic Dream
summary: Chinese tech giant NetEase Games is acquiring Quantic Dream, the developer behind titles like Heavy Rain and Detroit: Become Human, for an undisclosed amount. The acquisition marks Quantic Dream's first studio in Europe, with NetEase aiming to expand its global operations. Despite the acquisition, Quantic Dream will continue to operate independently, leveraging NetEase's resources to develop new narrative-driven games, including an upcoming Star Wars title.

title: Tencent and Sony Collectively Buy 30.34 percent of FromSoftware
summary: Tencent Holdings, through its subsidiary Sixjoy Hong Kong, and Sony Group, via Sony Interactive Entertainment, have jointly acquired 30.34% of FromSoftware. Sony now owns 14.09% and Tencent owns 16.25% of the company, with Kadokawa Corporation retaining 69.66%. This strategic investment aims to strengthen FromSoftware's development capabilities, expand its publishing scope in the global market, and capitalize on the success of titles like Elden Ring.

title: 3 Quantum Computing Stocks That Could 10X by 2030
summary: This article highlights three quantum computing investment opportunities – the Defiance Quantum ETF (QTUM), Honeywell International (HON), and IonQ (IONQ) – that could offer significant returns by 2030. It discusses the disruptive potential of quantum technology across various industries and its rapidly growing market valuation. The article provides an overview of each investment, outlining their current performance, key developments, and analyst forecasts for their future growth.

title: China gaming giants Tencent, NetEase invest in foreign studios
summary: Chinese gaming giants Tencent and NetEase are expanding their investments in overseas studios due to a slowdown in the domestic market. Tencent will acquire a 16.25% stake in Japan's FromSoftware, while NetEase has acquired French developer Quantic Dream. These moves highlight a continued pivot by Chinese tech companies towards international markets amid domestic regulatory crackdowns.

title: Netflix seeking premium prices for brands to advertise on its new tier
summary: Netflix is reportedly seeking premium prices for advertisers on its upcoming ad-supported platform, aiming for a cost per thousand viewers (CPM) of approximately $65. This pricing strategy suggests Netflix anticipates high demand from brands eager to reach its audience. The new ad-supported tier may launch as early as November 1.

title: DAX-ETF statt MSCI-World-ETF? Was der Fokus auf deutsche Aktien wirklich bringt
summary: This article examines whether a DAX-ETF is a viable alternative or supplement to an MSCI World-ETF for investors. The author argues that while German companies in the DAX have a long history, focusing solely on a DAX-ETF has historically yielded poorer returns compared to the more diversified MSCI World. Key reasons cited against a DAX-ETF include its historical underperformance, regional concentration, lack of tech companies, and limited number of constituent stocks.

title: DXC Technology’s Karim Jeribi on working with Lloyd’s, Manchester United, and digital transformation
summary: Karim Jeribi, VP of Sales for EMEA at DXC Technology, discusses the company's transformation and customer-centric approach, highlighting its work with clients like Lloyd's of London, Manchester United, and various automotive and banking sectors. He explains DXC's role in modernizing IT infrastructure, driving innovation, and differentiating itself from competitors through a holistic service offering and a "Cloud Right" strategy. Jeribi also touches upon the company's focus on talent development and its long-standing customer relationships.

title: Focus Cloud Acquires Microsoft, ServiceNow Cloud Talent Provider Cognitive Group -
summary: IT recruiting firm Focus Cloud has acquired Microsoft specialist Cognitive Group to form the new Focus Cloud Group. This expands Focus Cloud's recruitment expertise across major cloud platforms including Microsoft, Workday, SAP, Salesforce, and ServiceNow, as well as the life sciences and cybersecurity industries. The acquisition aims to build a global cloud recruitment powerhouse and grow internationally while benefiting shareholders and staff.

title: HP, Dell report cooling PC sales as business demand wavers
summary: HP and Dell have reported a decline in enterprise demand for PCs, signaling the end of the pandemic-era boom in the PC market. This downturn is attributed to economic uncertainty, with businesses delaying and reducing orders. Despite the current cooling, analysts believe the PC market's long-term floor is higher than pre-COVID levels due to hybrid work and hardware replacement cycles.

title: NEOS S&P 500 High Income ETF (SPYI) Price, Holdings, & News
summary: The NEOS S&P 500 High Income ETF (SPYI) is an exchange-traded fund launched on August 30, 2022, focusing on tax-efficient and high monthly income by investing in S&P 500 stocks and options. It employs a call spread approach using SPX index option futures contracts and has seen a 3.2% increase in stock price since the beginning of the year, currently trading at $54.18. The ETF's key holdings include major technology companies like Apple, NVIDIA, and Microsoft, and it maintains a dividend yield of 11.35% with a net expense ratio of 0.68%.

title: Formerly Sacred Now Rotting Silicon Valley Dictum of “Growth at All Costs” Crushes Okta: Shares Collapse 80% from Peak
summary: Okta, a company that provides secure access to cloud-based systems, has seen its shares collapse by 80% from their February 2021 peak after reporting a $210 million net loss and lowering its guidance. Despite consistent and growing annual net losses exceeding $2 billion, executives and analysts have ironically reframed these as "profitability," highlighting a prevailing Silicon Valley mantra of "growth at all costs." The company's struggles are attributed to "sales challenges" and "integration challenges" related to its 2021 acquisition of Auth0, signaling the potential end of an era for this business model.

title: Export Development Canada leads Canadian business toward a sustainable—and prosperous—cloud-based future
summary: Export Development Canada (EDC) is utilizing Microsoft Azure Cloud Services to embed environmental, social, and governance (ESG) principles into its core business and help Canadian companies become more sustainable. This digital transformation is reducing EDC's operational carbon footprint, improving disaster recovery, and enhancing employee productivity. Furthermore, EDC plans to use Azure's capabilities to track ESG metrics for its customers, encouraging decarbonization and supporting Canada's clean technology sector.

title: Qualcomm to supply custom chips for Meta’s virtual reality headsets
summary: Qualcomm Inc. and Meta Platforms Inc. have announced a multiyear strategic agreement for Qualcomm to supply custom chips for Meta’s Quest series of virtual reality headsets. These custom processors will be powered by Snapdragon XR platforms and technology and are designed to run Meta's Presence Platform, which facilitates mixed reality application development. This partnership is crucial for Meta's metaverse development efforts, with the custom chips potentially featuring AI optimizations to enhance the Presence Platform's AI components as Meta plans to release several new VR headsets by 2024.

title: Self-driving tech firm Aurora mulls sale to Apple or Microsoft - Bloomberg News
summary: Aurora Innovation Inc CEO Chris Urmson is exploring strategic options for the self-driving tech company, including a potential sale to Apple or Microsoft, to navigate challenging market conditions. Other considerations include cost cuts, going private, spinning off assets, and acquiring smaller companies. The company's shares rose 15% on the news but have suffered significantly this year, and it recently delayed the delivery of its autonomous freight trucks.

title: Microsoft, VMware, Ivanti Lead UEM Market As Hybrid Work Takes Over
summary: Gartner's 2022 Magic Quadrant for Unified Endpoint Management (UEM) tools identifies Microsoft, VMware, and Ivanti as global market leaders, driven by the increasing adoption of cloud-based UEM and hybrid work models. The report highlights strengths and weaknesses of six key vendors—Microsoft, VMware, Ivanti, IBM, ManageEngine, and Matrix42—predicting that over 90% of clients will use cloud-based UEM by 2025. This shift is also expected to lead to the convergence of UEM and digital employee experience tools by 2027, significantly reducing human effort in endpoint management.

title: Software superpower India to join world data capitals: Microsoft Corp president Brad Smith
summary: Microsoft Corp president Brad Smith states that India has become a software superpower and is poised to become one of the world's great data capitals, joining the top 2-3 software economies globally. He highlights India's significant digital progress, its influential role in technology regulation, and its potential to export its software stack to other countries, citing initiatives like ONDC, Aadhaar, and UPI. Smith also notes that India's growing working-age population presents an opportunity amidst an aging workforce in other major economies, and he emphasizes Microsoft's commitment to supporting India's digital growth.

title: Jim Chanos Takes Aim at Data Centers and Their High Valuations
summary: Noted contrarian investor Jim Chanos is challenging the high valuations of data center REITs, despite their apparent growth potential. He argues that major cloud providers building their own facilities pose a competitive threat, potentially limiting future growth for companies like Equinix and Digital Realty Trust. Chanos and other analysts also raise concerns about rising costs, intense competition, and opaque valuation metrics for these firms.

title: Baidu Announces Superconducting Quantum Computer and Integration Solution
summary: Baidu has unveiled its first quantum computing processor, Qian Shi, a 10-qubit superconducting quantum device, and a comprehensive "all-platform" integration solution called Liang Xi. Liang Xi aims to simplify access to quantum hardware resources via mobile, desktop, and the Cloud, making quantum computing more accessible for researchers and companies. Baidu's quantum software stack includes Quanlse for quantum control, Paddle Quantum for quantum machine learning, and Quantum Leaf for programming and simulating quantum computers.

title: Google CEO wants company to be 20% more efficient, hints at cuts
summary: Google CEO Sundar Pichai has indicated that the company needs to become 20% more efficient, hinting at potential cuts. This comes after Google previously announced plans to invest over $75 million locally. The move suggests a focus on cost-cutting measures, following a period where the company had added 10,000 employees in the second quarter.

title: NetApp Gets Into The MSP Game Via Spot, CloudJumper
summary: NetApp is expanding its focus into managed services by leveraging its Spot and CloudJumper acquisitions, particularly targeting MSPs with a cloud-first approach. The company is bundling its technologies with Microsoft Azure services to offer fixed-price, per-seat managed services, aiming to provide predictable margins and scalability for MSPs. This strategy deviates from NetApp's traditional storage focus, with Spot PC and CloudCheckr's CMX platform now serving hundreds of MSPs.

title: Sales Per Square Foot: Retail Calculations & Metrics (2024)
summary: This article explains the retail metric "sales per square foot," detailing its calculation and importance for brick-and-mortar stores. It covers how this metric helps measure store performance, inform merchandising decisions, analyze staff productivity, and identify sales trends over time. The article also discusses the limitations of sales per square foot, particularly in the age of omnichannel retail, and provides strategies to increase it, such as improving store layout, building loyalty programs, and leveraging online audiences.

title: The Head of Google Says Future AI Must Align with Human Values
summary: Google CEO Sundar Pichai emphasized at the Code 2022 conference that the future development of artificial intelligence must align with human values. He highlighted Google's strides in AI, including large language models and AlphaFold, but acknowledged that true "conversational AI" is still some years away and that Google needs to improve its handling of AI ethics. Pichai also discussed competition in the tech industry, antitrust concerns, content moderation, and the company's approach to issues like data privacy post-Roe v. Wade.

title: How to Buy NASDAQ Stocks
summary: This article provides a comprehensive guide on how to buy NASDAQ stocks, detailing what the NASDAQ is, who owns its shares, and the pros and cons of investing in them. It covers the steps to purchase NASDAQ stocks, from fixing a budget and choosing a broker to placing an order, and includes a brief history of the exchange. The article also mentions specific index funds and prominent companies listed on the NASDAQ.

title: How Telecom Argentina is evolving its B2B segment
summary: Telecom Argentina is aggressively expanding its B2B segment, with 38% of June revenues coming from cloud, cybersecurity, SD-WAN, and IoT solutions, a significant increase from 5% two years prior. The company has invested US$5bn in digital transformation between 2017 and 2021 to become a technology company and is also pursuing international expansion of its B2B services, particularly cybersecurity under the Ubiquo brand in neighboring countries.

title: Air Emissions Report Confirms Constellation Produces the Most Carbon-Free Electricity and Has the Cleanest Generation Fleet Among Large Power Producers
summary: An independent analysis confirms that Constellation, the nation’s largest producer of carbon-free energy, has the lowest rate of carbon dioxide emissions among the 20 largest investor-owned power producers in the U.S. Their fleet of nuclear, solar, wind, and hydro plants produces about 10 percent of the nation's carbon-free energy. Constellation is committed to producing 100 percent of its electricity from carbon-free resources by 2040 and is investing in new technologies like hydrogen production and direct air capture.

title: Insight Partners Backs Microsoft 365 Security Provider SaaS Alerts
summary: Insight Partners has invested $22 million in SaaS Alerts, a cybersecurity company that provides cloud application security software primarily to Managed Service Providers (MSPs). Founded in 2020, SaaS Alerts helps MSPs monitor and protect end-customers using various SaaS applications like Microsoft 365, Google Workspace, and Salesforce. This investment underscores Insight Partners' continued interest in the SaaS security and MSP software sectors, where it has several other related portfolio companies.

title: The B2B Content Guide: Tech Buyers Need Relevant Vendor Content Pre- And Post-Sales
summary: This article highlights the critical need for relevant B2B content at every stage of the tech buyer's journey, both pre- and post-sales. It discusses how current vendor content often falls short in relevance and credibility, leading to buyer disappointment. The article introduces a five-part blog series aimed at providing marketers with best practices for creating effective content strategies that address customer needs throughout their lifecycle.

title: Single-Stock ETFs Are Mushrooming. What to Know.
summary: Direxion, a fund company, is expanding its single-stock ETF offerings with six new funds. These ETFs will allow investors to make short-term bullish or bearish bets on major tech companies like Amazon, Alphabet, and Microsoft. This move signifies a further expansion in the fast-growing market of single-stock funds.

title: Remote Workplace Services Market Size, Industry Share Forecast
summary: The Remote Workplace Services Market is projected to grow from USD 20.1 billion in 2022 to USD 58.5 billion by 2027, at a CAGR of 23.8%. This growth is driven by increased employee engagement initiatives, cost reduction opportunities, and improved productivity stemming from remote work adoption, a trend accelerated by the COVID-19 pandemic. North America currently holds the largest market share, with key players including Wipro, HCL Technologies, and IBM.

title: Buy stocks with wide moats to protect your profits
summary: The article discusses Warren Buffett's "economic moat" concept, highlighting companies with sustainable competitive advantages. It outlines five key characteristics of such companies—intangible assets, cost advantage, switching costs, network effects, and efficient scale—and provides examples like Coca-Cola, Salesforce, and Alphabet. The piece concludes with advice on how investors can identify and invest in these wide-moat companies, including building a personal portfolio or using ETFs and investment trusts.

title: Trimble to purchase France-based PAg spraying company
summary: Trimble Inc., a California-based technology company, is acquiring Bilberry, a French manufacturer of selective weed spraying systems. Bilberry's AI and camera system, the Intelligent Spot Spraying System, identifies weeds in real-time and significantly reduces herbicide usage. This acquisition will enhance Trimble’s crop protection portfolio, adding green-on-green selective spraying capabilities and supporting their autonomous solutions development.

title: Will there be an end to the soda price increase? Not likely. Here's why.
summary: The cost of soda has increased by over 45% in less than four years, with a 12-pack now retailing for upwards of $7. Consumers like Rachel Hatfield and Rebecca Dunn find these prices "ridiculous" and "stupid money," forcing them to cut back on purchases despite inflation. The rise in prices is attributed to inflation, increased aluminum costs, and the lack of significant competition between beverage giants PepsiCo and Coca-Cola, suggesting that these price hikes are likely to continue.

title: The Scholastic Art & Writing Awards Open Entries as the Program Celebrates 100 Years of Recognizing The Nation's Creative Teens
summary: The Scholastic Art & Writing Awards have opened entries for their 100th annual program, inviting students in grades 7-12 from the U.S. and Canada to submit original works. In celebration of its centennial, the program, administered by the Alliance for Young Artists & Writers, announced nearly half a million dollars in scholarships, including increased portfolio awards and the inaugural Dav Pilkey Awards. These awards will recognize 12 high school seniors and their educators for outstanding portfolios, continuing the program's legacy of fostering young creative talent.

title: Microsoft, Lululemon take lead scooping up downtown Vancouver office space in 2022
summary: In 2022, Microsoft Corp. and Lululemon Athletica Inc. have become major acquirers of downtown Vancouver office space, leading to a stabilization in the market despite increased vacancy rates due to new building deliveries. Microsoft secured 468,000 square feet, while Lululemon leased 237,000 square feet, indicating strong demand for top-quality office space. This activity suggests that the current abundance of office space in Vancouver's downtown core will likely be short-lived.

title: PLDT to build new Aurora cable landing station
summary: PLDT Inc. announced plans to construct a new cable landing station in Baler, Aurora, and integrate the Asia Direct Cable (ADC) system by 2024. These initiatives are part of a broader strategy to enhance the Philippines' information and communication technology infrastructure, specifically targeting the growing hyperscaler industry. PLDT aims to position the Philippines as a leading hyperscaler hub in the Asia-Pacific region by expanding its data center operations and subsea cable capabilities.

title: News | Tech Companies Still Need Offices. But Here's How Their Look and Location Are Changing.
summary: Tech companies are rethinking their office real estate strategies, moving away from large, centralized headquarters to more flexible, dispersed models. Influenced by the pandemic shift to remote and hybrid work, companies like Salesforce and Google are opting for smaller, more purposeful spaces, often with enhanced amenities, or expanding to satellite offices in various cities. This change reflects a balancing act between cost-saving, attracting talent, and recognizing the value of in-person collaboration, while also acknowledging a broader geographic distribution of the tech workforce.

title: Microsoft integrates Israeli tech to upgrade video streaming quality
summary: Microsoft has launched new video streaming technology for its Teams platform, based on developments from Israeli firm Peer5, which Microsoft acquired a year ago. The technology, created at Microsoft's R&D center in Herzliya, aims to significantly improve the quality of large-scale live broadcasts without overloading networks, enabling organizations to host events for millions of users simultaneously. This integration is designed to support remote work environments by enhancing internal communication through high-quality virtual meetings and training sessions.

title: The miracle of streaming
summary: The article discusses the transformative impact of streaming technology on the world, from early internet speeds to today's high-resolution video consumption and its role in daily life and global data usage. It explores the history, underlying technology, and future implications of streaming, including its integration with AR/VR, 5G, and the Internet of Things, highlighting how networking has enabled this "miracle."

title: Small Business UCaaS M&A: Ooma Acquires OnSip -
summary: Ooma has acquired OnSip, a unified communications service provider specializing in small businesses, for $9.75 million in cash. This acquisition aims to expand Ooma's leadership in serving SMB customers and accelerate growth for Ooma Business. The article also provides context on the broader UCaaS market, noting some signs of consolidation and slowing M&A activity in 2022.

title: UnitedHealth Group’s Ann Williamson: Protecting privacy through security
summary: Ann Williamson, Chief Privacy Officer and Deputy General of UnitedHealth Group, discusses the critical link between privacy and security, stemming from her diverse career path in tech and law. She emphasizes that an effective privacy program is impossible without a robust security program and highlights the importance of collaboration between privacy and security teams. Williamson is also passionate about mentoring women in technology, advocating for training successful women from other fields to address cybersecurity staff shortages.

title: Oracle meets revenue targets on Cerner boost, cloud strength
summary: Oracle Corp met its first-quarter revenue targets, boosted by the acquisition of healthcare IT firm Cerner and strong demand for its cloud services. Cerner contributed $1.4 billion to revenue, helping to offset a slowdown in business spending. Oracle expects revenue growth of 21% to 23% in the second quarter on a constant currency basis.

title: Oracle offers its MySQL HeatWave database and analytics on Amazon’s cloud
summary: Oracle has made its MySQL HeatWave cloud database service available on Amazon's AWS cloud, allowing customers to use the service without migrating their data from AWS. This move enables Oracle to reach customers who have historically stored their data on AWS, even though Oracle directly competes with Amazon's database services. Oracle also plans to offer this database platform on Microsoft's Azure cloud in the future.

title: Gartner Survey Shows 75% of Organisations Are Pursuing Security Vendor Consolidation in 2022
summary: A Gartner survey reveals that 75% of organizations are pursuing security vendor consolidation in 2022, a significant increase from 29% in 2020. The primary driver for this consolidation is to improve risk posture and reduce complexity, rather than solely to cut costs. Opportunities for consolidation are seen in areas like SASE and XDR, with many organizations planning to adopt these technologies by the end of 2022.

title: Ministry of Justice moves official website into Microsoft cloud
summary: The Ministry of Justice in Qatar has migrated its official website to the Microsoft cloud, in collaboration with the Ministry of Communications and Information Technology (MCIT). This move is part of Qatar's digital transformation plan, aligning with Qatar National Vision 2030, and follows the launch of Microsoft's first large-scale cloud data center in Qatar. The migration aims to accelerate digital procedures, promote legal culture, and develop the community.

title: 343 Industries founder Bonnie Ross resigns after leading Halo brand for 15 years
summary: Bonnie Ross, the founder of 343 Industries, has announced her departure from the company and Microsoft after 15 years, citing a "family medical issue." Her role will be split among three individuals as part of a restructuring to manage the Halo franchise's future development and cross-media efforts. This resignation follows other notable departures from the studio, including the Halo Infinite art director and several design leads.

title: Plenty of Robinhood Stocks Found in These ETFs
summary: The article discusses how many popular stocks among Robinhood users are also found in prominent ETFs like the Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ) and Invesco NASDAQ 100 ETF (QQQM). Robinhood's newly introduced Robinhood Investor Index, which tracks the top 100 stocks in client portfolios, reveals that a significant portion consists of large-cap names and stocks in the communication services, consumer discretionary, and technology sectors, aligning with the holdings of QQQ and QQQM. This suggests Robinhood users may be more practical in their investment choices than their "meme stock" reputation implies.

title: Tech stocks crushed in market selloff
summary: The six largest U.S. tech companies collectively lost over $500 billion in value following an unexpectedly high August inflation report. The Nasdaq Composite experienced its steepest drop since June 2020, sinking 5.16%. Major companies like Apple, Microsoft, Amazon, Alphabet, Meta, and Nvidia saw significant declines, with the report potentially influencing further aggressive interest rate hikes from the Fed.

title: Cloud optimization co Zesty raises $75m
summary: Israeli cloud optimization company Zesty has raised $75 million in a Series B funding round co-led by B Capital and Sapphire Ventures, bringing its total funding to $116 million. The company's automated system dynamically adjusts cloud configurations to ensure stability and optimize performance rather than solely focusing on cost reduction. Zesty has doubled its annual recurring revenue since early 2022 and employs 120 people, serving over 300 customers with most revenue from North America.

title: Microsoft patches a new zero-day affecting all versions of Windows
summary: Microsoft has issued security patches for a zero-day vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2022-37969, impacting all supported Windows versions, including Windows 11 and earlier, and Windows Server. This elevation of privilege flaw, which allows attackers to gain system privileges, has been exploited in real-world attacks. Additionally, Microsoft addressed another zero-day, CVE-2022-23960, a cache speculation vulnerability affecting Windows 11 for ARM-based systems, as part of its monthly Patch Tuesday release.

title: Arm unveils updated Neoverse CPU roadmap, targeting cloud, hyperscale and HPC workloads
summary: Arm has announced an updated Neoverse CPU roadmap to provide a foundation for various workloads in cloud, hyperscale, and high-performance computing. The new Neoverse V2, codenamed Demeter, aims to deliver top per-thread performance and power efficiency, with partners like Nvidia already integrating it. Additionally, Arm detailed upcoming N-series and E-series chip designs set for a 2023 launch, catering to different compute needs prioritizing thread count or data plane processing.

title: WSJ News Exclusive | Netflix Estimates Ad-Supported Tier Will Reach 40 Million Viewers by Late 2023
summary: Netflix projects that its upcoming ad-supported streaming tier will attract approximately 40 million global viewers by the third quarter of 2023. This estimate was shared with ad buyers as Netflix and Microsoft, its advertising partner, seek to finalize deals ahead of the planned launch. The move comes after Netflix experienced its first subscriber decline in nearly a decade.

title: Rigetti Expands QCS™ Availability to Microsoft’s Azure Quantum Platform
summary: Rigetti Computing has launched its QCS™ platform in Public Preview on Microsoft’s Azure Quantum platform, making its 80-qubit Aspen-M-2 and 40-qubit Aspen-11 quantum processors accessible to all Azure Quantum users. This integration allows developers to use Rigetti's proprietary Quil language and supports popular quantum programming frameworks, enhancing flexibility and performance optimization. Rigetti is also participating in the Azure Quantum Credit program, providing users with credits to explore its QPUs.

title: Matter, Sidewalk, Wi-SUN, Wi-Fi 6 – new Silicon Labs range for IoT in home, yard, city
summary: Silicon Labs has unveiled four new solutions as part of its Series 2 portfolio, aiming to accelerate the "mega-cycle in IoT" across various applications from smart homes to smart cities. These new offerings include development kits and chip systems supporting Matter, Amazon Sidewalk, Wi-SUN, and Wi-Fi 6, addressing the growing demand for mature and integrated IoT platforms. The company anticipates 27 billion IoT devices by 2025 and has doubled its IoT revenue in the last three years, positioning itself to be a key player in this expanding market.

title: Emerge EMPWR Unified Sustainable Equity ETF
summary: This article provides a detailed profile of the Emerge EMPWR Unified Sustainable Equity ETF (EMPW), noting it is no longer active. It covers key financial data, including its expense ratio, inception date, AUM, and historical trading data. The profile also lists its top holdings, concentration analysis, performance metrics, geographic and sector exposures, and technical indicators, offering a comprehensive overview for investors.

title: Blameless announces integrations with ServiceNow and Microsoft Teams
summary: Blameless has announced new integrations with ServiceNow and Microsoft Teams to enhance its incident management platform for enterprise customers, streamlining workflows and improving incident response. These integrations centralize incident management, automate channel creation, and provide real-time updates and reliability insights, ultimately reducing workload on engineering teams. This move helps Blameless expand its presence in the enterprise SaaS market and further invest in DevOps and IT workflow tooling.

title: To Infinity and Beyond!
summary: This article explores the futuristic concept of space-based data centers, following the current trend of underwater data centers. It discusses the potential advantages of such an endeavor, including cost reduction, natural cooling, and improved disk drive performance in zero-gravity environments. However, it also highlights the significant challenges, primarily the need for completely maintenance-free systems and the risks associated with the harsh space environment.

title: Author: Vamsi Nekkanti
summary: This page profiles Vamsi Nekkanti, an author at Sify, and highlights his article "Data Centers To Infinity and Beyond!". Nekkanti, a technology enthusiast from Visakhapatnam, focuses on the future of data centers, including innovative concepts like underwater and space-based data centers, and mentions Microsoft's patent for an Artificial Reef Data Center. The page also lists other recent articles discussing AI, deepfakes, and data center innovations.

title: Turtle Beach Debuts Its First Mobile Gaming Controller With the Designed for Xbox Recon Cloud Hybrid Controller
summary: Turtle Beach has unveiled its first mobile gaming controller, the Designed for Xbox Recon Cloud Hybrid Controller, expanding its controller lineup. This new device targets mobile gamers using compatible Android devices, Xbox, and PC, offering over 30 hours of battery life. When wired to consoles or PCs, it provides exclusive Turtle Beach audio features like Superhuman Hearing, custom audio presets, and more.

title: IT services inflation follows broader market trend
summary: CIOs should expect increased costs for IT consulting and professional services, a trend that reflects broader market inflation driven by rising labor costs across various service sectors. While hardware costs have stabilized or declined, professional services have seen a steady increase since early 2021, prompting Gartner to advise CIOs on strategic cost management rather than reactive budget cuts to avoid detrimental business impacts.

title: Lawsuit Accuses Zillow, Microsoft Of ‘Wiretapping’
summary: A class action lawsuit has been filed against Zillow and Microsoft in Washington state, alleging that Zillow's website uses embedded code from Microsoft and other vendors to "wiretap" visitors' online interactions. The suit claims this code records mouse movements, clicks, keystrokes, and other communications, creating a video replay of user behavior that violates privacy rights and the state's wiretapping statute. Plaintiffs are seeking civil remedies, while Zillow states it is reviewing the lawsuit and is transparent with its privacy policy.

title: What’s New in Artificial Intelligence from the 2022 Gartner Hype Cycle™
summary: The 2022 Gartner Hype Cycle for Artificial Intelligence highlights key AI innovations expected to drive significant business benefits and will see mainstream adoption within two to five years. These innovations are categorized into data-centric, model-centric, applications-centric, and human-centric AI, with a focus on impact on both business leaders and engineering teams. The article emphasizes technologies like composite AI, decision intelligence, edge AI, and responsible AI as crucial for competitive advantage and solving complex business problems.

title: Strive 500 ETF (STRV) Price, Holdings, & News
summary: This article provides a detailed overview of the Strive 500 ETF (STRV), including its current price, holdings, and news. It outlines the ETF's investment strategy, expense ratio, top holdings like NVIDIA and Apple, and recent news headlines related to its performance and capital attraction. The piece serves as a comprehensive resource for potential investors interested in the STRV ETF.

title: 6 customer self-service best practices
summary: This article outlines six best practices for optimizing customer self-service, emphasizing its role in improving customer experience (CX) and sales. Key recommendations include continuously updating knowledge bases, identifying common customer issues suitable for self-service, and utilizing virtual assistants to guide customers. The piece also stresses the importance of offering omnichannel capabilities, embracing AI technologies for maintenance, and systematically measuring the success of self-service strategies to ensure they meet organizational goals.

title: Rigetti Announces New Partnerships and Details Multi-Year Roadmap Designed to Reach Quantum Advantage
summary: Rigetti Computing, Inc. announced an updated multi-year roadmap and key partnerships at its inaugural investor day, focusing on achieving Quantum Advantage. The roadmap includes the upcoming Ankaa™ 84-qubit system and Lyra™ 336-qubit system, alongside collaborations with companies like Keysight, NVIDIA, Bluefors, and Microsoft Azure to enhance hardware, software, and climate modeling applications. Rigetti is also expanding its Fab-1 facility and developing next-generation cryogenic platforms.

title: S&P 500 could see another '10-15% correction downwards': Strategist
summary: Ann Berry, founder of Threadneedle Ventures, predicts the S&P 500 could face another 10-15% correction due to macroeconomic challenges like the strong dollar, rising energy prices in Europe, and persistent inflation concerns. Despite the gloomy outlook, she suggests opportunities for value stock picking, particularly in companies like Netflix that have credible turnaround plans, and stable companies with good dividends for long-term retail investors. The market is seen as under-pricing broader macro issues beyond just Fed rate hikes.

title: Expert: Zillow Privacy Lawsuit Has Wider Implications
summary: A civil lawsuit filed against Zillow Group Inc. and Microsoft Corp. alleges privacy violations through the collection of user interaction data on Zillow's website, including mouse movements and keystrokes. An expert in internet privacy law suggests this case, and similar ones, could force significant changes in how companies draft their privacy policies and collect user data. The core issue revolves around the vagueness of Zillow's privacy policy and whether it adequately discloses the extent of data collection to consumers.

title: How CrowdStrike plans to become a generational platform
summary: CrowdStrike Holdings Inc. has rapidly become a leading security firm, boasting over $2 billion in annual recurring revenue and a $40 billion market capitalization, with projections to reach $5 billion in revenue by mid-decade. The company's success is attributed to its architectural platform, strong go-to-market strategies, and strategic acquisitions, positioning it as a potential generational platform in the cybersecurity sector, despite broader market headwinds. The article delves into CrowdStrike's platform, customer spending momentum, and its focus on extended detection and response (XDR) as it aims to consolidate point products in the market.

title: The making of TSMC and its ecosystem
summary: TSMC has solidified its dominant position in the global wafer foundry market due to its advanced technology and strategic ecosystem development, securing orders from major IC designers worldwide. Despite global economic headwinds, TSMC projects significant revenue growth and continues massive expansion projects, fostering extensive collaborations with its supply chain partners through initiatives like the Open Innovation Platform. The company faces competition in advanced process nodes but maintains a leading edge through strong client relationships and continuous investment in technological advancements.

title: Off to the (24) races: F1 is capitalizing on its growing audience
summary: Formula 1 announced a record-breaking 24-race calendar for 2023, showcasing its growing global audience, particularly in the US. This expansion follows Liberty Media's acquisition in 2017 and strategic moves like the Netflix series "Drive To Survive," which significantly boosted viewership and interest. The new schedule includes an inaugural Las Vegas Grand Prix, marking a substantial push into the American market.

title: Salesforce unveils Genie, a real-time data platform to power its apps
summary: Salesforce Inc. has unveiled Salesforce Genie, a new real-time data platform designed to power its entire suite of customer relationship management products. Genie aims to unify and personalize customer data in real-time, enabling highly personalized experiences across marketing, sales, and commerce, and addressing data fragmentation issues caused by numerous separate applications.

title: NVIDIA Introduces DLSS 3 With Breakthrough AI-Powered Frame Generation for up to 4x Performance
summary: NVIDIA has introduced DLSS 3, an AI-powered performance multiplier that leverages neural rendering to significantly boost frame rates by up to 4x compared to brute-force rendering, while maintaining image quality. This technology, powered by new fourth-generation Tensor Cores and an Optical Flow Accelerator on GeForce RTX 40 Series GPUs, generates entire new frames using AI, even benefiting CPU-limited games. Over 35 games and applications, including major titles and game engines like Unity and Unreal Engine, are slated to support DLSS 3.

title: Most common SAP vulnerabilities attackers try to exploit
summary: Attackers are consistently targeting SAP applications due to unpatched systems, misconfigurations, and vulnerable custom code, exploiting known critical vulnerabilities often within days of disclosure. Organizations struggle with patching all identified SAP vulnerabilities, leading to exposure to data theft and system disruptions. Key vulnerabilities include specific CVEs like RECON and Invoker Servlet flaws, as well as configuration errors like weak passwords and custom code injection flaws.

title: Serverless Data Centers – Wave of the future?
